helps.title: Your learning
helps.what: Your quizzes, mock exams, flashcards and AM2 practice in one place, with the topics to work on next.
steps: Practise what you got wrong: Practise next lists the topics where you have the lowest share of right answers across every quiz and mock. Practise your weak spots builds a paper from them.
Clear your flashcards: Cards come back when they are due. Reviewing them little and often is what makes them stick.
Do what your tutor set: Quizzes your tutor set appear here with their date. Open one to start or carry on.
Keep the AM2 in view: The AM2 card shows how many sections you have at the practice bar. Open the simulator to run one.
notes: Your figures, not a forecast: Every number here comes from what you have done in the app. Nothing on this page predicts a grade.

helps.title: Me
helps.what: Your details, your college and tutor, and the two ways to send your portfolio out: export it or share a private link.
steps: Check your course: The course under your name is the one your portfolio is marked against. Your college sets it if you are enrolled.
Talk to your tutor: Comments on your evidence and messages to your tutor are both here.
Export or share: Export my record builds a ZIP with a PDF summary and every file. A share link lets someone view your portfolio without an account.
notes: Your record stays yours: You can export it at any time, including after you finish or change college.

helps.title: Do next
helps.what: Everything that is waiting on you, in one list, with the thing that costs most to leave at the top. Your college, your assessor and the app all feed it.
steps: Start at the top: Overdue work, criteria your assessor sent back and a review to sign come first. Then anything due this week, then the rest.
Tap the row: Each item opens the exact place to deal with it: capture with the criteria already ticked, the quiz, the hours to confirm, the message thread.
It clears itself: Send the evidence, confirm the hours or sign the review and the item drops off. Nothing to tick here.
notes: Nothing on the list?: You get the one thing that would help most this week, worked out from your course: the unit with the biggest gap, or your off-the-job hours if you are behind.
No college?: The list still works. Your portfolio, assessor feedback and witness statements are yours, college or not.

helps.title: Your portfolio
helps.what: Everything you have captured for your qualification, what each piece covers, where it stands with your assessor, and what to do next. Your record stays yours.
steps: Capture: Add a photo, document or note from site. The AI may suggest criteria; they only count once you claim them.
Use your own electrical work: A certificate, a schedule of test results or a calculation you did in Elec-Mate becomes evidence in two taps, with a readable copy and suggested criteria.
Claim and get it witnessed: Open the evidence, claim each criterion it really shows, and ask the supervisor who saw you do it to sign.
Do what your tutor set: Items under "From your tutor" are your assessment plan. Tap Capture this and the criteria are ticked for you. Each one ticks itself off when you send that evidence.
Sign and send: Submit for assessment with your declaration that it is your own work. Your assessor passes it or asks for more.
Send again when asked: If your assessor needs more, read their feedback in the evidence, add to it and send it again.
notes: Only passed counts: Your progress figure is criteria your assessor has passed. Claimed and submitted are shown separately so you always know what is still to be judged.
Export your record any time: Export my record builds a ZIP with a designed PDF summary, every file, your declarations, hours and the audit trail. Packs are kept; download links last 24 hours.
Nothing is lost or changed quietly: Every file carries a fingerprint (SHA-256) and every change, claim, decision and signature is kept in an audit trail you and your assessor can read.

helps.title: Coverage
helps.what: Every criterion on your course and where each one stands. The ring shows the whole course; each unit shows its own bar.
steps: Read the ring: Green is passed by your assessor. Blue is with your assessor. Orange needs more. White is claimed or suggested. Grey is not started.
Filter by state: Tap a line in the key, for example Not started, to see only those criteria. Tap it again to show everything.
Open a unit: Each criterion shows its state, any feedback and the evidence it is tied to. Capture for unit starts new evidence aimed at the gaps.
notes: The same figures your assessor sees: Coverage reads the same record as your assessor and your tutor, so the numbers always agree.

helps.title: Readiness
helps.what: How close your record is to the end of your programme: criteria passed, off-the-job hours, evidence someone has seen, and your tutor's plan.
steps: Check the rings: Each ring is a real figure from your record. Tap one to see the detail behind it.
Work down Before gateway: Each line says what your record shows today and the one thing to do next.
Clear what needs you: Evidence waiting on a step from you is listed with that step. Tap it to open the evidence.
Write your statement: A few sentences in your own words. It opens your exported record.
notes: Not a grade or a prediction: Your tutor and employer decide when you are ready for gateway. This page only shows what your record says.

helps.title: College access
helps.what: Your college uses the College Hub through an agreement with Elec-Mate. When that agreement ends, the hub pauses until it is renewed.
steps: Nothing is deleted: Learners, cohorts, evidence, hours and records all stay exactly as they are.
Talk to Elec-Mate: Your college lead can email founder@elec-mate.com to carry on.
Back where you left off: As soon as access is renewed, the hub opens again with everything in place.

helps.title: The assessment hub
helps.what: Where assessors work: everything waiting to be assessed at the top, where your learners stand beside it, and every assessment tool below.
steps: Clear the queue: Evidence, written quiz answers, hours, app learning, IQA verdicts and reviews to write up. Each button opens the exact item.
Check where learners are: Attendance, plan reviews overdue and who is at gateway, each one tap from the detail.
Use the tools: Grading, registers, learning plans, EPA, IQA and reports, grouped by job.

helps.title: People
helps.what: Everyone your college works with: learners and their cohorts, tutors and support staff, employers, and the courses they are enrolled on.
steps: Find someone fast: Find someone searches learners and staff together. The search in the top bar (⌘K on a keyboard) finds learners from any screen.
Start with who is at risk: The list says why each learner is flagged. Tap one to open their Student 360 and act on it.
Check your cohorts: Each cohort card shows its learners, attendance and who is at risk. Tap one for the roster filtered to that group.
Run the college: The cards at the bottom go to staff, workload, employers, courses, bulk jobs and settings.
notes: Risk scores: Risk is worked out from attendance, progress, portfolio activity and observations. Refresh risk scores recalculates them for the learners listed.

helps.title: Curriculum
helps.what: Everything you need to plan and teach: courses, schemes of work, lesson plans, the timetable and the materials you teach from.
steps: Plan the year: Set up the course, then a scheme of work that spreads the units across the weeks for a cohort.
Plan each lesson: Write or generate a lesson plan, map it to the assessment criteria, and build the slides from it.
Teach and take the register: Open the lesson from Next 7 days, deliver it, and take the register from the same screen.
notes: Drafts: A lesson plan stays a draft until you mark it ready. Drafts show in orange so nothing is left half-written before the class.

helps.title: Quality and compliance
helps.what: Everything that keeps the college safe and inspection-ready in one place: safeguarding, internal quality assurance (IQA), staff checks, policies, and the documents an inspector or auditor will ask for.
steps: Start with Needs you: Everything waiting on someone, most urgent first. Orange means it needs doing; tap a row to go straight to it.
Keep the cycle moving: Sample work for IQA, rehearse an inspection, draft the self-assessment or update the improvement plan from Start something.
Keep the paper trail: Staff checks, policies, reports and the audit log are under Records, ready to print or download.
notes: Safeguarding: Designated safeguarding leads and their deputies see and act on concerns. If the college has no lead with an account, admins and heads of department are told instead and can see and act on them until a lead is set. Everyone else sees who the leads are and how to raise one.
Staff checks: In date, expiring within 60 days, awaiting verification, expired, or missing, from the single central record. The same states and colours are used in Compliance docs and the audit pack.

helps.title: Resources and admin
helps.what: The records an inspector asks for, the materials your tutors teach from, and the settings that connect the college to other systems.
steps: Keep records in date: Compliance docs shows DBS checks, policies and staff records that have expired, are missing or are about to expire.
Share materials: Teaching resources and the document library hold slides, handouts, templates and policies everyone can use.
Connect your systems: Link a VLE (Canvas, Moodle or any LTI 1.3 platform) and invite employers to see their apprentices.

helps.title: Portfolios
helps.what: Every learner’s portfolio in one place: the evidence waiting for your decision, oldest first, and how far each learner is through their criteria.
steps: Clear what is waiting: Each row is evidence a learner has sent for assessment. Tap it to open their criteria in Student 360 and record passed, needs more or not yet. The learner sees your decision straight away.
Check progress: The learner list shows criteria passed out of the total for their qualification, when they last added evidence and anything still waiting. Filter to find learners who have gone quiet.
Set extra requirements or check the gateway: The slider button on a learner row opens extra evidence requirements for that learner and their EPA gateway checklist.
Sample for IQA: Internal quality assurance sampling, verdicts and actions live on the IQA page, linked at the bottom.
notes: My learners or the whole college: My learners are those in cohorts you tutor, or where you are named tutor, assessor or IQA. The switch is shared with every College Hub screen.
Learners who have not joined: Their evidence lives in their own Elec-Mate account, so they show no criteria until they join with the cohort code.

helps.title: Draft learning plans
helps.what: Drafts an individual learning plan for a learner from what their record already holds: attendance, criteria coverage, observations, off-the-job hours, end-point judgements and any earlier plan. It is written by AI; you review and edit it before anything is saved.
steps: Start at the top: Learners with no plan come first, then overdue reviews, then by risk.
Draft and review: Tap a learner. The draft streams in; change any goal or strategy before you save.
Save to their plan: Saving writes the plan and goals to the learner's record, where you review it with them.

helps.title: The assessment calendar
helps.what: Every assessment date for your learners on one month: observations, professional discussions, portfolio reviews and gateway meetings you book here, plus gateway and EPA dates from the EPA records.
steps: Pick a day: Tap a day on the month to see what is on it. Today is outlined; a dot means something is booked.
Schedule an assessment: Choose the learner, the type, the date and time, and where it happens. It appears on the calendar straight away.
Open the learner: Tap any row to open that learner’s record. Gateway and EPA dates open the gateway board.
notes: My learners: Shows learners in the cohorts you lead. Switch to Whole college for the whole college.

helps.title: Registers and attendance
helps.what: Take the register for a class in two taps, fix a mark after the event, and see which learners are below 85% attendance.
steps: Take the register: Tap "Take a register" or the class under Today. Your cohort, today's date and your name are already filled in.
Mark the exceptions: Tap "Everyone else here", then tap Late, Absent or Authorised for anyone who is not. Every tap saves. Undo puts the last change back.
Follow up: Learners below 85% are listed with their rate. Tap one to open their record and log the conversation.
notes: How the rate works: Present and Late count as attended. Absent and Authorised do not. A learner with no marks has no rate yet.
One mark a session: A learner has one mark for the morning and one for the afternoon. Taking the same session again updates its marks. Rates count sessions, not days.
Changing a mark: Open a day under Registers and tap a learner to change their mark or add a note.

helps.title: Audit log
helps.what: A permanent record of the sensitive things staff do in the College Hub: who did it, when, and to which record. Inspectors and awarding bodies can ask you to prove an action happened; this is where you show them.
steps: Narrow it down: Search by name, or pick an action, a record type and a date range.
Read an entry: Each line says what happened, who did it and when. Extra detail recorded with the action shows underneath.
Download the evidence: Download CSV saves exactly what is on screen, ready to attach to an audit or inspection pack.
notes: Nothing can be deleted: The log is append-only. No one, including admins, can edit or remove an entry.
Who can see it: Admins, heads of department, IQAs and quality nominees at your college.
Dates: Entries are grouped by UK date (Europe/London), so an action just after midnight in summer time sits on the right day.

helps.title: Bulk jobs
helps.what: Do one job for a whole cohort in one pass: record the same grade for many learners, clear overdue ILP reviews, or send everyone a message.
steps: Pick the cohort: The first active cohort is picked for you. The number beside each is its active learners.
Pick the job: Record grades, ILP reviews (with how many are overdue), or Message the cohort.
Check and run: The line above the button says exactly what will happen and to whom before you tap it.
notes: ILP reviews: Marking a plan reviewed stamps today and sets the next review … weeks out.
Messages: Only learners with an app account receive a message. The confirmation says how many were skipped.

helps.title: Cohorts
helps.what: Your class groups. Each card shows how many learners are in it against its places, their attendance, who is at risk, and how much of their qualification has been passed.
steps: Open a cohort: Tap a card for the roster filtered to that cohort, with every learner's figures.
Take its register: Register on a card opens the register for that cohort, ready to mark.
Message everyone: Message sends one note to every learner in the cohort.
Compare: Compare cohorts puts up to three side by side: progress, attendance, off-the-job hours and EPA readiness.
notes: Of criteria passed: Assessment criteria an assessor has passed, across every learner in the cohort who has joined, out of all the criteria on their qualification. The same count each learner sees in their portfolio.
Adding a cohort: New cohort needs a course (set one up in Course setup first), a name, a code and a lead tutor. Learners join it with its join code, or you enrol them from Learners.

helps.title: Your college home
helps.what: Your day in one place: the class you are teaching next, everything waiting on you, your learners by cohort, and every other part of the College Hub.
steps: Start with today: Open the lesson to teach from it, or take the register in two taps.
Clear what needs you: Hours to verify, evidence to review, messages and marking, oldest and most urgent first. Filter by type at the top.
Check on your learners: Each cohort shows attendance, who could do with a check-in, and the next class.
Find everything else: Assess, Teach, Apprenticeship rules and College group every other page, each with a line on what it is for.

helps.title: College settings
helps.what: Where your college sets the rules the rest of the hub uses: attendance targets, how much IQA samples, what the lesson planner should always include, and your VLE connection.
steps: Quality thresholds: The attendance target that flags a learner, the IQA sampling rate, how far back inspection signals look, EPA verdicts and the risk flags. Changes reach every screen within a second.
Lesson plan settings: British values, stretch and challenge, inclusion and safeguarding context that every generated lesson plan includes.
VLE integration: Connect Canvas, Moodle or Blackboard so learners launch Elec-Mate from your VLE.
Microsoft Teams: A college admin or head of department pastes a Teams Workflows webhook link. New tutor inbox items then post to that channel, held overnight, each with a link back into the hub.

Your notifications: Choose which pushes reach your phone: marking, hours, messages, reviews. Each one opens the exact item. Anything you switch off still appears in the bell. Safeguarding always comes through.
notes: Who can change these: Everyone at your college can read them. Any staff member can change lesson plan settings; only a college admin or head of department can change the quality thresholds and risk flags. Each change is saved for the whole college. Your notifications are the exception: they are yours alone.

helps.title: Staff records and policies
helps.what: The single central record for every member of staff (DBS, right to work, references, declarations) and the college policies staff must read and sign. Inspectors ask for both on day one.
steps: Fix what is red first: Expired and missing records are the ones an inspector will find. Tap a person to upload the document, add the expiry date and the reference number.
Verify what is uploaded: A record someone else uploaded shows as awaiting verification until a second person checks the original and signs it off.
Keep policies live and read: Switch to Policies to add one, start from a template, or draft one. Publish it and staff are asked to acknowledge it; the log is kept for you.
notes: Where these records come from: Each staff member has the statutory checks their role needs. Add staff under People and they appear here automatically.

helps.title: Course setup
helps.what: The courses your college runs: what learners enrol on. Each course carries the off-the-job hours its apprenticeship standard needs, and every learner enrolled on it inherits that target.
steps: Add a course: Pick its qualification first: that fills in the name, code, awarding body and level for you.
Set the standard: Choose the apprenticeship standard it delivers. That sets the off-the-job hours. Choose Custom to type hours yourself.
Keep it tidy: Mark a course Inactive when you stop running it. Learners already on it keep their record.
notes: Off-the-job target not set: Learners on a course with no target have nothing to measure their hours against. Set it once here.

helps.title: Qualifications
helps.what: Every electrical qualification in the catalogue, broken down into units, learning outcomes and assessment criteria, each linked to the BS 7671 regulations it touches.
steps: Find the qualification: Search by code or title, or narrow by level and awarding body.
Open a unit: Each unit lists its learning outcomes and assessment criteria.
Tap a criterion: See the regulations, Guidance Note 3 and On-Site Guide sections that match it, and generate a lesson plan from it.
notes: Courses you run: This is the catalogue. The courses your learners enrol on, and their off-the-job hours, are set in Course setup.

helps.title: Criteria gaps
helps.what: Every assessment criterion of the class’s qualification, with how many learners have it passed, with the assessor, sent back, claimed or nothing yet. The weakest unit comes first, so you can see in seconds what to teach next.
steps: Pick the class: My cohorts puts every cohort you are the tutor on together. Tap a cohort to look at just that class.
Open the weakest unit: Units are ordered by the share of criteria passed, lowest first. Each criterion shows a bar and, in words, how many have nothing yet.

Plan a lesson for the gaps: Tick the criteria you want to teach and tap Plan a lesson for these. The lesson planner opens with those criteria and the cohort already picked. A lesson covers one unit, so ticking a criterion in another unit starts a new selection.
See who is where: Tap a criterion for the learners and where each one is on it. Tap a learner for their profile.
notes: Where the figures come from: Each learner’s portfolio record of every criterion, the same one their portfolio and the assessor use. Passed includes IQA confirmed. With the assessor includes a pass an IQA has queried. Sent back is referred or not yet. Claimed means the learner tagged evidence but has not sent it. Nothing yet includes criteria with only an AI suggestion.
Who is counted: Learners on the cohort who have joined the app and are not withdrawn or completed. Learners you are not allowed to see are left out and said so.

helps.title: Document library
helps.what: Every document, slide deck, video and link the college has shared, in one place to search and open.
steps: Find it: Search by title, description or tag, or pick a type to narrow the list.
Open it: Tap a document to preview it here without leaving the app.
Add more: Upload goes to Teaching resources, so there is one place to add and tag files.
notes: Storage: The college has 5 GB. When it is nearly full the figure turns orange; delete old files to make room.

helps.title: EPA admin
helps.what: The end-point assessment record for every apprentice: where they are in the pipeline, their gateway and EPA dates, and the result once they have sat it.
steps: Add a record: When an apprentice enters the pipeline, add their EPA record. Move them along as they go.
Hold the gateway meeting: From a learner’s menu, open the gateway meeting: tick the checklist, set the date and notes.

Check what is missing: Heading to EPA lists each apprentice with a date, nearest first, with how many gateway lines are met and the first one still open. Gateway readiness has every line, each a link to where it is fixed.
notes: Where the gateway figures come from: From the gateway check itself: minimum time on programme, off-the-job hours, criteria passed, English and maths, the NET checklist and the signed declarations. The stage on an EPA record is what someone set; the gateway lines are what the record shows.
Sort by forecast, filter Off pace: Soonest forecast lists the records by gateway forecast, earliest first. Off pace keeps everyone behind or close to their planned end.

helps.title: Employers
helps.what: Every employer your apprentices work for, with how their apprentices are doing: attendance, criteria passed, off-the-job hours and reviews.
steps: Open an employer: Tap an employer to see their apprentices. Tap an apprentice for their Student 360.
Share a link with them: Set up share link gives the employer a page with their apprentices' progress, no account needed.
Keep reviews moving: Apprentices due a review are listed. Progress reviews books and records the three-way review with the employer.
notes: Off-the-job on track: An apprentice is on track when their verified hours are within 90% of where they should be by now.
Workplace visits: Record a site visit as an observation on the learner's profile; it keeps the same evidence trail.

helps.title: Grading
helps.what: Every assessment your learners have handed in, with the oldest unmarked at the top. Mark it, add feedback, or send it back for resubmission.
steps: Mark the oldest first: The list opens on To mark, oldest first. Anything over a week is orange.
Open, then grade: Tap a row to see the submission. The menu on the right grades with a rubric, quick-grades, adds feedback or asks for a resubmission.
Record one from scratch: Record a grade adds an assessment that was marked away from the app.
notes: Keyboard: On a desktop: j and k move down and up the list, Enter opens the highlighted assessment.
Whose work: My learners shows the cohorts you lead or learners assigned to you. Whole college shows everyone at the college.

helps.title: Learning plans
helps.what: Every learner’s current individual learning plan: its targets, how many are met, and when the plan is next reviewed. Overdue reviews sit on the right so nothing slips.
steps: Clear overdue reviews: The list on the right is every plan whose review date has passed, oldest first. Tap one to open the plan and review it.
Read the charts: Review status and plan status are tappable: tap a bar to filter the list to just those plans.
Create a plan: Create an ILP lets you pick a learner and build their plan. It is the same plan Student 360 shows.
notes: My learners: Opens on the cohorts you lead. Switch to Everyone for the whole college.

helps.title: IQA workflow
helps.what: A one-page view of internal quality assurance: how much of each assessor's work has been sampled, the findings and actions that came out of it, standardisation meetings, and readiness for the next external quality assurance (EQA) visit.
steps: Check sampling: Each bar is one assessor: how much of their work has been sampled against the target. Orange means behind. Set plans and give verdicts on the IQA dashboard.
Log findings and close them: Add a finding for good practice, something to improve, or an action required. Tap it to close it when it is resolved.
Record standardisation: Log each standardisation meeting with the number who attended and what was agreed.
Get ready for the EQA: Set the visit date and tick off the evidence checklist as each item is ready.

helps.title: Off-the-job audit
helps.what: An internal quality check on off-the-job hours. You sample entries an assessor has already verified and say whether you agree with their decision, so the hours you claim for funding stand up.
steps: Pick an entry: The list shows verified entries waiting for an IQA check, oldest sign-off first by days. Tap one to read it and what the assessor said.
Give your verdict: Agree, partial agreement, disagree or escalate. Add feedback for the assessor. You cannot record a disagree or escalate verdict without it.

Flag a follow-up: Switch on follow-up required when something needs doing. It marks the verdict as needing follow-up on the audit record; it does not create a task, so agree the next step with the assessor.
notes: Assessor agreement: How often you agreed with each assessor over the last 90 days. Below 70% is a sign they need standardisation or support.

helps.title: VLE integration
helps.what: Connect your VLE (Canvas, Moodle or Blackboard) so learners and staff open Elec-Mate from it with one sign-in, and grades and rosters can flow between the two.
steps: Add the platform: Add platform asks for your VLE's details. Or use Install with one URL if your VLE supports dynamic registration.
Give your VLE admin our details: Tool configuration lists the URLs and keys your VLE needs. Each has a copy button.
Verify and watch launches: Verify the connection, then Health and launches shows every launch and any that failed, with the reason.
notes: Setup guides: Step-by-step guides for each VLE are under Setup guides.

helps.title: Lesson plans
helps.what: Every lesson plan you and the college have written, with when it is taught and whether it is ready.
steps: Start a plan: New plan asks who it is for and which unit, then drafts the plan from the unit assessment criteria.
Finish and mark ready: Open a draft, check the objectives, timings and activities, then mark it ready to teach. Build the slides from the same screen.
Teach it: Next to teach shows the next lesson in the timetable. Deliver opens the presenter view. Mark it delivered afterwards.
notes: Mine and Everyone: The list opens on your own plans. Tap Everyone to see the whole college.

Not marked delivered: The lesson date has passed but nobody marked it delivered. Taking its register on or after the lesson date marks it delivered. Otherwise tap Mark delivered on the card, or open it and re-date it.

helps.title: Off-the-job training
helps.what: Every apprentice’s off-the-job hours against the fixed total their standard requires, and whether they are on pace to reach it by the planned end date.
steps: Start with who is behind: The list is sorted furthest behind first. Tap an apprentice to open their hours in Student 360.
Clear what is waiting: Hours learners log wait in Hours to verify; time spent learning in the app waits in Approve app learning. Both are at the top of the page.
Check the monthly rule: Funding rules expect some off-the-job training every calendar month. The figure shows who has none yet this month.
notes: The figure: Counted hours are verified hours plus app learning not yet approved: the same figure Student 360, the cohort hours page and the apprentice’s own app show.
Whose apprentices: The switch at the top picks Mine, My cohorts or Whole college for the whole College Hub.

helps.title: Progress tracking
helps.what: Every active learner’s progress score, attendance and risk flag in one place, so you can see who is on track and who needs you before it shows up at gateway.
steps: Start with who is at risk: Learners flagged Critical, High or Medium sit on the right, worst first. Tap one to open their Student 360.

Read the spread: The charts show how many criteria your learners have passed, whether that is on pace for how far through the programme they are, and how each cohort compares. Tap a bar or a cohort to filter the list.
Assess or contact: The … on a row opens their criteria to assess, gives a quick view, or calls or emails them.
notes: Where the figure comes from: Criteria passed counts every criterion an assessor has passed or an IQA has confirmed, out of the total for the learner’s qualification. It is the same count as their portfolio and Student 360. Learners who have not joined the app have no criteria yet.
My learners: Opens on the cohorts you lead. Switch to Everyone for the whole college.
Export: Export CSV downloads the list exactly as it is filtered.

helps.title: Quality dashboard
helps.what: The college’s headline quality figures, each against its target, with the learners who need you and the evidence an inspector will ask to see behind each number.
steps: Read the figures: Each figure shows how far it is above or below target. Orange means below target. Tap a figure to open the records behind it.
Work through Needs you: Low attendance, overdue learning plan reviews, EPA gateways and marking, each one tap from the list to fix.
Contact learners at risk: Each flagged learner shows why, in plain words, and what to do. Log contact once you have spoken to them; it is saved as a 1-2-1 note on their record.
Download the report: Download PDF makes a clean copy of these figures, the learners at risk and the attendance trend to hand over.
notes: How the figures are worked out: Attendance: present or late out of every register mark. Learning plans: active learners reviewed in the last six weeks. Achievement: completed out of everyone who has left. Retention: active and completed out of everyone who started.

EPA on track: For each active learner: the share of their qualification’s criteria passed (or IQA confirmed), against the share of their time on programme gone from start date to expected end date. A learner is on pace when the share passed is no more than 10 percentage points behind the share of time gone. Learners with no start or end date, or no qualification with criteria, are left out and said so.

Risk levels: Worked out overnight from coverage against time on programme, off-the-job hours, portfolio, observations, attendance and open pastoral flags. Critical and high are listed; contacted means a 1-2-1 or intervention note since the learner was flagged.

helps.title: Resource use
helps.what: Which teaching resources learners actually open and download, so you know what is working and what to replace.
steps: See what is used: The chart shows the most-used resources. Change the measure with the chips: views, unique viewers or downloads.
Mark the best: Mark a resource as gold standard so other tutors know it is the one to use.
Replace what is not: Resources nobody opens are worth replacing or removing from Teaching resources.

helps.title: Safeguarding
helps.what: Where safeguarding concerns about learners go, and, for designated safeguarding leads, the list of every concern logged at the college.
steps: Raise a concern: Open the learner’s record, add a note and choose Safeguarding. It is saved as a restricted note and sent straight to the designated leads.
Leads acknowledge it: A lead taps Acknowledge so everyone can see it has been seen. Unacknowledged concerns are shown in orange at the top.
Act and record: Open the learner record to see the full history and record what was done.

Record the decision: Record your decision and the reasons, any referral to children’s social care, the LADO or Channel with its date and reference, and whether the learner has a social worker. Leads only.
When a learner leaves: Learners who leave with a safeguarding record appear under Child protection files. Send the file securely within 5 days and record the confirmation of receipt.
notes: Restricted notes: Safeguarding notes are visible only to designated leads and their deputies. Tutors, including the person who logged it, cannot read them back from the learner record.

Under 18: Learners who were under 18 on the day of the concern are children in law. Their concerns are flagged so the lead can follow the procedures for a minor, including telling the employer’s responsible person where appropriate. A learner with no date of birth on file shows as Age unknown, because their age can’t be checked.

No lead set?: If the college has no active designated lead or deputy with an account, concerns go to admins and heads of department instead, and they can read, acknowledge and close them until a lead is set. If there are none of those either, nobody is told. Set a lead in Compliance docs.

helps.title: Schemes of work
helps.what: A scheme of work spreads a qualification across the year for one cohort: which unit is taught in which week. Inspectors and quality reviews ask to see one for every group.
steps: Create a scheme: Pick the qualification, the cohort and the start and end dates.
Plan its lessons: Open the scheme to see the cohort's lessons dated inside it, week by week, and which units still have criteria no lesson covers. Plan a lesson for the cohort from there.
Set it active: An active scheme shows how far through the year the cohort is. Archive it when the year ends.
notes: Drafts: A draft is not shown as a cohort's plan yet. Set it active once the weeks are planned.

helps.title: The learner profile
helps.what: Everything the college holds on one learner. The name line shows their employer and tutor. The overview shows four figures, what needs you and a card for each part of the record; tap a card to open that part on its own page.
steps: Start with Needs you: Anything late or waiting on you for this learner, most costly first. Each row opens the place to deal with it.
Open a card: Each card shows the headline figure. Tap it for the full detail: criteria, hours, reviews, portfolio and the rest.
Record as you go: Start something logs a one-to-one, a note, an observation or a grade without leaving the profile.
Step through a cohort: The arrows by the name, or Ctrl and the arrow keys, move to the next learner and keep the page you are on.
notes: Orange means look now: A card turns orange when something is behind: hours off course, a review due inside two weeks, goals past their date, attendance under 85%.
Last contact: Days since the newest message you sent, one-to-one, observation or held progress review. It turns orange after four weeks.
Charts on a phone: On a phone the charts and trends sit under the cards. Tap Charts, trends and details to open them.
Back to the overview: Use Overview at the top of any area, or your browser back button.

helps.title: Learners
helps.what: Everyone on your roll, with the figures that tell you who needs you: risk, attendance, off-the-job hours and progress. Tap a learner to open their Student 360.
steps: Start with yours: The switch at the top shows your learners first: the ones assigned to you and the cohorts you teach. Switch to the whole college when you need everyone.
Filter to what matters: Tap a chip to narrow the list: at risk, low attendance, behind on hours, or one cohort.
Open the learner: Tap a row for Student 360. The ⋯ menu has call, email, assign staff, edit, and the moves: change cohort, break in learning, withdraw or completed.

Message a group: Filter the list (behind on hours, a cohort) and tap "Message these", or Select the learners you want. Write one message and each learner gets their own copy with their own figures in it. You read every message in the preview before anything is sent.
Add learners: Enrol one at a time, paste a whole class with Bulk enrol (you see every row checked before anything is saved), or share a join code.
notes: Attendance: Counts present and late against every register marked. A learner with no register yet shows a dash, never 100%.
Off-the-job hours: Counted hours against the hours their programme needs, the same figure as the Off-the-job page.

Criteria passed: Assessment criteria an assessor has passed, out of every criterion on their qualification: the same count the learner sees in their portfolio. "Not joined" means the learner has no account linked yet, so there is no portfolio to count.

helps.title: Support staff
helps.what: Everyone who is not teaching: assessors, internal quality assurers (IQA), administrators and learner support.
steps: Add someone: Add staff member takes a name, email, role and department. It does not make a login: give them one from Add several with logins on the Tutors page.
Filter by role: The chips narrow the list to assessors, IQA, admin or support.
Open a profile: Tap a row for their details, qualifications and contact. Compliance checks are in the ⋯ menu.
notes: Assessors and IQA: An assessor or IQA needs their qualification on file (for example TAQA, IQA award) before they sign off evidence. Put it on their profile.

helps.title: Teaching resources
helps.what: The college's shared library of slides, handouts, videos and links. Anything here can be attached to a lesson and mapped to the assessment criteria it covers.
steps: Add to the library: Upload files (or drag them onto the list on a computer), or add a link to a video or web page.
Tag and map: Open a resource to give it tags and map it to the assessment criteria it teaches.
Use it in lessons: Search by title or tag and attach it to a lesson plan, so learners see it with the lesson.
notes: Who sees what: Everything here is shared with staff at your college.

helps.title: Timetable
helps.what: Every lesson with a date, laid out as a week. On a computer you see the whole week by time; on a phone you see a list, day by day.
steps: Your week first: It opens on your own lessons. Tap "Everyone" to see the whole college, or a tutor to see theirs.
Open a lesson: Tap a lesson to open its plan, slides and register.
Take the register: Today's lessons have a Register button. Your cohort and the date are already filled in.
notes: Where lessons come from: A lesson shows here once its plan has a date. Add a start time and length to place it in the week grid; without one it sits at the top of the day.

helps.title: Learner notebook
helps.what: Ask a question about a learner and get an answer written from their real record: criteria met, quizzes, off-the-job hours, observations and end-point judgements. It is AI, so check anything you act on.
steps: Pick a learner: Tap a learner to open the notebook with their record loaded.
Ask, or use a ready question: Gateway readiness, biggest gaps, a 1-2-1 agenda or what to observe next.
Check and use it: Answers say where they came from. Copy what is useful into a review, a learning plan or your notes.
notes: Who you see: Your assigned learners first. If none are assigned to you, everyone at the college.

helps.title: Lesson observations
helps.what: Every observation of a tutor’s teaching in one place: peer, IQA, head of department, learning walks and standardisation. Use it to make sure every tutor is observed at least once a year and that actions are followed up.
steps: Check who is due: Tutors with no observation in the last 12 months sit at the top in orange. Arrange an observation for them first; this page records observations, it does not book them.
Look at the spread: The charts show the grades given and the kinds of observation, so you can see whether it is all peer reviews or a proper mix.
Read the detail: Tap an observation to see the focus, strengths, development points and agreed actions.
notes: Awaiting tutor: The tutor has not yet acknowledged the write-up. Ask them to read and sign it.
Developmental: An ungraded observation for development only.

helps.title: Tutor workload
helps.what: How much each tutor is carrying: cohorts, lessons this week, marking waiting and how long since they were observed. Use it to spread the load before someone tips over.
steps: Look at the orange and red: Overloaded tutors are at the top. Move a cohort or some marking to someone balanced.
Check observations: A tutor with no observation in a year is flagged. Book one; inspectors ask for it.
Go to the person: Tap a tutor to open the Tutors page, where their profile and cohorts are.

helps.title: Tutors
helps.what: Your teaching team: who teaches which cohorts, how many learners each has, and how much marking is waiting with them.
steps: Onboard a starter: Walks you through a new tutor: details, qualifications, then their compliance checks (DBS, CPD, qualifications on file).
Add one: Name, email and department when you need someone on the list now. It does not make a login.

Add several with logins: Paste one line per person. Anyone new gets a login; anyone who already has an Elec-Mate account gets a staff join link by email. You see every row checked before anything is saved.
Open a tutor: Tap a row for their profile, qualifications and contact details. Edit from there.
Balance the load: Workload shows every tutor's cohorts, lessons this week and marking side by side.

helps.title: Work queue
helps.what: The assessment jobs waiting on tutors: grades to record, learning plan reviews that are overdue, learners near gateway and evidence to assess. It reads like the inbox, longest waiting first.
steps: Start at the top: Anything past its due date, marked urgent or waiting a week or more is under Waiting too long, the same rule the inbox uses.
Open the item: The button says what to do: Grade, Review, Check or Assess. Evidence opens the submission itself; the others open the screen where the work is done.
Keep your own place: Mark items as started or done, or add a note, from the ... menu. That is your own record; the item leaves the queue when the work itself is done.
Many at once: Tick rows and Start or Complete them together. On a computer: j and k move, Enter opens, s starts, c completes, x ticks.
notes: Whose work: The switch at the top picks Mine, My cohorts or Whole college for the whole College Hub.
The inbox: Off-the-job hours, messages, comments and progress reviews are in the inbox, not here.

helps.title: Assessment plan
helps.what: What you have asked this learner to evidence next. Each item names the criteria, how to show them, a suggested activity and a date. The learner sees it as a to-do with a button straight into capture.
steps: Set a plan item: Pick the criteria (those that need more and those not started come first), choose how they should be evidenced, write the activity in plain words and set a date.
The learner is told: They get a notification that opens the item. Their capture sheet starts with your criteria ticked.
It closes itself: When they send evidence claiming every criterion on the item, or you pass those criteria, the item is marked done and you are told.
Overdue items: An item past its date shows on your home and inbox as a check-in, urgent after a week.
notes: You can still close it yourself: Mark done if the evidence came another way, cancel if it no longer applies, or reopen a closed item.

helps.title: Automations
helps.what: Ready-made rules for the jobs you repeat every week: draft the invoice when a job is done, chase an unpaid invoice, remind people about timesheets. Every rule is off until you turn it on, and everything a rule does is logged.
steps: Pick a rule: Each rule reads as a sentence. Tap it to see exactly what it does and what it would act on right now.
Turn it on: Tap the switch. Rules that email your customers or touch money ask you to confirm, and only the owner or an admin can turn those on.
Check the run log: Every run, skip and failure is listed with the reason, and also shows on the job and in the audit log.

tasks.title: Turn a rule on
steps: Find the rule. Tap it to read what it will do.
Tap Turn on. For rules that email customers, read the safety notes and tap Turn on again to confirm.
tasks.who: Anyone in the office can turn on team and office rules. Rules that email customers or touch money: owner and admins only.

tasks.title: Stop everything for a while
steps: Tap Pause all at the top.
Tap Resume all when you are ready.

tasks.title: See what a rule did
steps: Open Run log.
Each line says what happened, or why it was skipped. Tap Open job to go to the job.

notes: Nothing happens twice: Each rule acts once per job, invoice, certificate or week. Moving a job back and forward again does not draft a second invoice.
Customer emails wait two minutes: So a crew booked together is one email, and so you can switch a rule off if you change your mind. The rule is checked again just before sending.
What the crew sees: Nothing to set up. They just get the results: a job pack to sign, or a reminder to log their hours.

helps.title: Checklists
helps.what: Set what the crew must tick, photograph and sign before they start a job and when they finish. Nobody can clock themselves in to a job until their required before-start checks are done, including signing the RAMS.
steps: Pick or build a checklist: Start from the Library (safe isolation, DB change, EICR visit, EV charger, PAT round) or tap New checklist.
Put it on jobs: Tap Attach to a job, or set the checklist to go on every new job or on jobs with a label.
Watch it fill in: The Jobs tab shows what is missing on each live job. Open one for the photos, signatures and a PDF for the client or the HSE.

tasks.title: Use a ready-made checklist
steps: Open the Library tab.
Tap Add to my checklists on the one you want.
It appears under Checklists, ready to edit or attach.

tasks.title: Build your own
steps: Tap New checklist.
Give it a name and say what kind of job it is for.
Add items under Before start and On completion. Pick the type: tick, photo, signature, number, yes/no or RAMS signed.
Leave Required on for anything that must be done. Turn on Supervisor countersigns for apprentices where you need it.
Choose when it goes on jobs automatically, then tap Save checklist.

tasks.title: Put a checklist on a job
steps: Tap Attach to a job.
Pick the job and the checklist, then tap Attach.

tasks.title: Prove the checks were done
steps: In the Jobs tab, tap the job.
Each person’s before-start checks and the job’s completion checks show who did them, when and where, with the photos and signatures.
Tap Download PDF for the client file or an HSE visit.

notes: Before start and On completion: Before-start checks are done by each person on the crew. On-completion checks are done once for the whole job, usually ending with the customer’s signature.
Changing a checklist: A job keeps the version it was given. Editing a checklist changes it for jobs it goes on from now, not ones already under way.
RAMS signed: This item reads the job pack sign-offs. If a pack was sent to the person for this job and they have not signed it, they cannot clock in.
The office clocking someone in: Only a worker clocking themselves in is held back. The office can still clock a person in from Timesheets.

helps.title: Clients
helps.what: Every customer in one place, with what they have paid, what they owe, open quotes, jobs and certificates. One record per customer for the whole firm.
steps: Add or find the client: Tap Add client, or search by name, company or email. Converting a lead also adds them here.
Open their record: Tap a client to see paid, outstanding and open quotes, plus their quotes, invoices, jobs and certificates.
Act from the record: Call, email, start a quote or job already filled in, share their portal, and keep follow-ups and notes.

tasks.title: Add a client
steps: Tap Add client.
Type the client name. Company, email, phone, address and notes are optional.
Tap Add client at the bottom.

tasks.title: See what a client owes
steps: Tap the client in the list. The amount due shows in amber on the right.
The record opens with Lifetime paid, Outstanding and Open quotes at the top.
Scroll to Invoices and tap one to open it.

tasks.title: Start a quote or job for them
steps: Open the client.
Tap New quote or New job.
Their name is filled in for you (and email, phone and address on a quote). Finish it as normal.

tasks.title: Share their portal
steps: Open the client.
In the Client portal card, tap Create portal link the first time.
Then Copy, Share, WhatsApp, Email or show the QR code.

tasks.title: Keep a follow-up or note
steps: Open the client and scroll to Follow-ups.
Type it in Add a follow-up, pick a date if you want, then tap Add. Tick it when done.
Under Activity, pick Note, Call, Email or Meeting, type what happened and tap Log.

tasks.title: Remove a client
steps: Open the client and scroll to the bottom.
Tap the bin, then Delete.

notes: Messages: A purple pill means the client has written to you from their portal. Open them to read and reply.
Who sees the totals: Office managers see how many clients owe money, not the firm-wide £ totals. Each client still shows their own balance so it can be chased.

helps.title: Leads
helps.what: Every enquiry from first contact to won, before it becomes a client. Requests from your quote page land here on their own.
steps: Get leads in: Share your quote page so requests arrive by themselves, or tap Add lead for a phone call or a referral.
Follow up: Open a lead and let Mate draft a text or email. Sending a follow-up moves a New lead to Contacted.
Win it: Move the stage as it goes. Convert to client marks it Won and adds them to Clients, ready to quote.

tasks.title: Add a lead by hand
steps: Tap Add lead.
Type the name or company. Contact, email, phone, source, estimated value and notes are optional.
Tap Add lead at the bottom. It starts as New.

tasks.title: Follow up with Mate
steps: Tap the lead.
Under Follow up with Mate, tap Text or Email. Mate writes a draft you can edit.
Tap Send text or Send email. Your phone opens the message ready to send, or tap Copy.

tasks.title: Move a lead along
steps: Open the lead.
Under Move stage, pick New, Contacted, Quoted, Won or Lost.
Use the tabs at the top to see each stage.

tasks.title: Turn a lead into a client and quote
steps: Open the lead and tap Convert to client.
It is marked Won and added to Clients (no duplicate if you tap twice).
Open it again and tap Write a quote. The quote opens with their name, email and phone.

notes: Win rate: Won out of everything decided (won plus lost). Open leads do not count. Quotes use the same rule, with expired quotes counted as decided.

helps.title: Clients
helps.what: Where work comes in and customers are kept. The figures are the same ones Finance uses, so they always match.
steps: Get work: Email, website, quote page, calls, texts and bookings all land in Enquiries.
Keep the customer: Win a lead and it becomes a client, with their quotes, invoices, jobs and balance on one record.
Let them see it: Client portal gives each client one private page with their jobs, certificates and invoices with Pay now.

tasks.title: Find your way round
steps: Quote page: your own page and QR code where customers ask for a quote.
Enquiries: every way a customer gets in touch, until the quote is accepted.
Clients: every customer and what they owe.
Quotes & Invoices: raise, send and chase. Tenders: bids for bigger work. Client portal: links and messages.
Review requests: one honest review request to each customer after they pay, with who clicked.

notes: The numbers: Outstanding is sent and overdue invoices not yet paid. Drafts never count. Tap a figure to open the page behind it.

helps.title: Smart Docs
helps.what: Every document a job has, in one place: RAMS, job pack, briefings, quotes and invoices, certificates and signatures, with who has signed. AI drafts the ones it still needs and you check them before they go anywhere.
steps: Pick a job: Under Start a document, pick the job in For a job. Each card then says whether the job has it, and its documents list below. Leave it on All jobs for the most recent across the firm.
Pick the document: Tap a card: Safety documents for RAMS and method statement, Design spec for a circuit design, AI quote for a priced draft quote.
Give it the job: Fill in the steps or pick a job. The more detail, the better the draft.
Check it: Nothing is final until you have read it. Edit, then download or send.

tasks.title: Draft a design spec
steps: Tap the Design spec card.
Work through Project, Supply, Circuits, Install, Validate and Review, tapping Next.
Tap Generate Design, then Download PDF from the results.

tasks.title: Draft a quote
steps: Tap the AI quote card.
Tap Start a draft, pick a job or describe the work, then Draft my quote.
Check the lines and tap Save draft and review. You send it from the quote builder.

notes: RAMS, method statements and briefing packs: The Safety documents and Briefing pack cards open the safety tools. They have their own help on each page.
Who sees the counts: Counts and the recent list cover documents made by the owner and managers.

helps.title: AI Design
helps.what: Design a whole installation for one of your jobs. Each circuit is sized, protected and checked. The design is saved to the job, where the crew can read it, and you can put its PDF in the job pack or quote from it.
steps: Pick the job: Under The job, pick the job. Its name, site and client fill in the first step, and the design is saved to it as soon as it starts.
Describe the job: Six steps: Project, Supply, Circuits, Install, Validate and Review. Tap Next to move on.
Generate: On Review, tap Generate Design. It works through every circuit and shows progress as it goes.
Check and download: Read each circuit and its workings, then tap Download PDF. New design starts again.

tasks.title: Design an installation
steps: Project: the basic details of the job.
Supply: the electrical supply characteristics.
Circuits: add each circuit. Install: how each one is run.
Validate runs a pre-flight check. Fix anything it flags, then Review.
Tap Generate Design.

tasks.title: Get the PDF
steps: When the results show, check each circuit.
Tap Download PDF. On a phone it opens so you can save or share it.
Tap New design to start another.

notes: You sign it off: The design is a draft to check against BS 7671 and site conditions. It does not replace your own judgement.

After the design: Open a saved design from the list. Add to job pack puts its PDF in the job’s pack. Start a quote opens a quote for the job with its cable and devices as lines, priced from the design for you to check.

helps.title: Settings
helps.what: Your firm details, managers, seats, branding, the office email, card payments, QS sign-off and the bank details printed on invoices.
steps: Fill in the company: Name, number, VAT, phone, email, website and address go on quotes, invoices and emails.
Brand it: Upload your logo and pick two colours. Save branding to apply them.
Get paid: Add bank details for invoices, and connect Stripe so every invoice has a Pay now link.

tasks.title: Update company details
steps: Open Company and change any field.
A bar appears at the bottom. Tap Save all, or Discard to undo.
tasks.who: The account owner. Managers can see settings but not change company details, branding or payments.

tasks.title: Add your logo and colours
steps: Under Branding, tap Upload and pick your logo (PNG, JPG or SVG).
Set the primary colour (buttons and accents) and secondary colour (headers).
Check the live preview, then tap Save branding.

tasks.title: Add a manager
steps: In Managers, tap Add manager.
Type the email they sign in with, and their name and job title if you like.
Pick Office or Admin, then tap Add manager.

tasks.title: Set up card payments
steps: In Card payments, tap Connect Stripe.
Stripe asks for business details, ID and the bank account to pay into.
If it says Setup not finished, tap Finish setup in Stripe.

tasks.title: Add your bank details to invoices
steps: Scroll to Billing & payments.
Fill in account name, sort code and account number.
Tap Save.

tasks.title: Turn on QS sign-off
steps: Scroll to QS sign-off.
Switch on Require QS approval before issue. Team EICR, EIC and Minor Works then need a QS countersignature before the PDF can be issued.
If you are the QS yourself, also switch on I am my own Qualifying Supervisor.

tasks.title: Get office emails
steps: Under Notifications, type the office email.
Tap Save next to it.

helps.title: Compliance
helps.what: One register for the documents that keep the firm trading: insurance, PAT, calibration, audits and permits, each with its renewal date. We remind you before anything lapses.
steps: Add each document: Tap Add document. Give it a name, a renewal date and attach the certificate if you have it.
We remind you: 30 days and 7 days before a renewal date, and again if it passes, a reminder lands in your bell and in the morning office email.
Renew it here: Open the document, tap Record renewal, set the new date and attach the new certificate.
Send the evidence: Evidence pack builds a PDF of your safety score and this register for SSIP and principal contractor questionnaires.

tasks.title: Record a renewal
steps: Tap the document in the register.
Tap Record renewal.
Set the new renewal date, attach the new certificate and tap Save.

tasks.title: Answer a pre-qualification questionnaire
steps: Tap Evidence pack at the top of the page.
Attach the PDF to the questionnaire, or send it to the main contractor.

notes: Who gets the reminders: The owner and every active admin. The morning email goes to the office email in Settings, on weekdays.
The safety score: Built in Site Safety from toolbox talks, near misses, countersigned records, COSHH reviews and RAMS. With too little on record it shows Not started, never 100.

helps.title: Job financials
helps.what: Profit per job: what you invoiced against labour, materials, expenses and other costs. Budgets sit alongside so you can see a job going wrong early.
steps: Find the job: Use the tabs to see jobs losing money, over budget or over their quoted hours. Tap a job to open it.
Read where the money went: Value, costs and invoices on one sheet. Labour comes from approved timesheets, materials from purchase orders, expenses from approved claims.
Add what is missing: Record a cost the app cannot see, correct the labour with a reason, set a budget or add a variation.

tasks.title: Find the jobs losing money
steps: Tap the Losing money tab. Over budget and Over quoted hours work the same way.
Tap a job to open its profit sheet.
Check Costs: labour, materials, expenses and other. Tap Labour to see the hours behind it.

tasks.title: Record a cost the app cannot see
steps: Tap the job, then Record cost.
Pick Materials, Equipment, Overheads or Other.
Enter the Amount (£), the Date of the cost and a note if you like.
Tap Record cost. It shows in the job’s Cost log.

tasks.title: Correct the labour on a job
steps: Tap the job, then Labour.
Type the figure in Set labour cost to (£).
Give a reason. It is required and kept in the job’s log.
Tap Save labour. To undo it, tap Go back to timesheet labour.

tasks.title: Add and approve a variation
steps: Tap the job, then Add variation.
Describe the extra work and enter the Value (£).
Tap Add variation. It shows under Variation orders as Pending.
Tap Approve on it when the client agrees. Only approved variations add to the contract value.

tasks.title: Set a budget
steps: Tap the job, then Edit budget.
Enter the figures you plan to spend.
Tap Save Budget.

tasks.title: Set what an hour of each person costs
steps: Tap Cost rates at the top.
Type a rate for each person: pay plus NI, pension, van and tools. Leave it blank to use their pay rate.
Tap Save on each row you change, then Done.

notes: Who sees it: Job profit, labour cost and budgets are for the owner and admins. Office managers see a note instead.
Same figures everywhere: Gross profit is invoiced less costs, the same maths as Reports and Accounts. Draft invoices are not counted.

helps.title: Reports
helps.what: Invoiced, costs and gross profit for a period, who owes you, and which jobs make money. The same figures as Accounts and Job financials.
steps: Pick a period: This month, last month, this quarter, this year, the last 12 months or all time.
Read the figures: Profit and loss, debtor aging and job profitability update for the period you pick.
Act on it: Tap a debtor row to chase overdue invoices, tap a job to open its profit, or export the profit and loss.

tasks.title: Get a profit and loss for a period
steps: Tap the period along the top, for example This quarter.
Read the Profit & loss card: invoiced, materials, expenses, labour and gross profit.
Tap Export CSV to download it for your accountant.
tasks.who: Owner and admins. Office managers see invoice figures only, and Export CSV stays off.

tasks.title: Chase who owes you
steps: Scroll to Debtor aging. Unpaid invoices are split by how late they are.
Tap a row with money in it to open your overdue invoices in Quotes & Invoices.

tasks.title: See which jobs make money
steps: Scroll to Job profitability. It shows your top 10 jobs by gross profit.
Tap a job to open it in Job financials.

notes: What counts: Invoiced means sent, overdue or paid. Drafts are left out. Expense claims are only a cost once approved.

helps.title: Signatures
helps.what: Every document your clients have been asked to sign, for the whole office: quotes, variations, handovers, certificates and contracts. The client reads the actual document on their phone and signs it with their finger. If they signed a printed copy instead, you record it here with a photo of the paper.
steps: Send a document: Use Request signature here, or Get it signed on a quote, a variation, a job or a contract. You see exactly what the client will see before you send.
Watch it come back: Each request shows whether it has been sent, opened, signed or declined. Chase by email once a day, or copy the link and text it.
Keep the signed copy: Download the signed copy: the document plus a signature page with the name, time, IP address, device and a fingerprint of the version signed.

tasks.title: Send a variation to sign
steps: Tap Request signature.
Under What they sign, tap Variation.
Pick the job. Say what is changing, choose Extra or Saving and type the price change.
Under Who signs, add the name and email. Leave the email blank to get a link to text yourself. Pick how long the link works: 7, 14 or 30 days.
Check What they will see, then tap Send for signature (or Create signing link).

tasks.title: Record a paper signature
steps: Open the request from the Waiting tab and tap Record a paper signature. (No request yet? Tap Request signature, then Signed on paper, and pick the document.)
Check the name of the person who signed and the date they signed. The date cannot be in the future.
Tap Take a photo to photograph the signed page, or Choose a file for a PDF scan.
Tick I confirm this is the client's signature on this document, then tap Record paper signature.

tasks.title: Chase a signature
steps: Open the Waiting tab and tap the request.
Tap Chase by email. You can chase once every 24 hours, up to 6 sends.
Or tap Copy link or Share and send it by text or WhatsApp.

tasks.title: Add a signed variation to the job value
steps: A green bar shows signed variations still to add. Tap it, or open the request from the Signed tab.
Tap Add £… to job value.
The job value goes up (or down for a saving) and the variation is approved in Job financials.

tasks.title: Download the signed copy
steps: Open the request from the Signed tab.
Tap Download signed copy. You get the document with a signature page: name, time, IP address, device and a fingerprint of the version signed.
For a paper signature the page says Signed on paper, who recorded it and when, and the scan of the paper follows it.

tasks.title: Cancel a link
steps: Open the request.
Tap Cancel this link, then Cancel link. It stops working straight away.

notes: Variations: A signed variation does not change the job value on its own. Open it and tap Add to job value when you are ready.
Links: A link works once, runs out after the days you choose, and you can cancel it. If the document changes after you send it, the client cannot sign the old version.

Signed on paper: If the client signed a printed copy, record it with a photo or PDF of the paper. It always shows as Signed on paper, recorded by whoever added it, with the scan attached. It is never shown as a digital signature, and once recorded it cannot be changed or deleted.

helps.title: Quotes and invoices
helps.what: Every quote and invoice for the firm in one list. Write a quote, send it for the customer to accept online, turn it into an invoice, then chase it until it is paid.
steps: Write the quote: Tap New quote. Fill in the client, labour and materials, then Send. The customer gets a PDF and a link to accept it.
They accept, you invoice: When the customer accepts you get a notification. Open the quote and tap Convert to invoice.
Get paid: Send the invoice, chase it from the Overdue tab, and tap Mark paid when the money lands.

tasks.title: Create and send a quote
steps: Tap New quote.
Client: add the client name (needed) and their email (needed to send it). Pick the deposit under Deposit on acceptance.
Tap Next. Add labour on Labour, then materials on Materials (Pick from the price book or type a line).
On Review, tap Send. Or Save draft to finish it later.

tasks.title: Take a deposit
steps: In the quote, under Deposit on acceptance, pick Percentage or Fixed amount and type it. Firm default uses the deposit set in Settings.
Send the quote.
When the customer accepts online they are asked to pay the deposit by card before the job is booked.
Open the quote: it shows Waiting for the deposit, then Deposit paid by card.

tasks.title: Send a draft quote, or send it again
steps: Tap the quote in the list.
On a draft, tap Send email. If there is no email on it, type one and send.
On a sent quote, use Get the customer link to copy the accept link and text it yourself.

tasks.title: Turn an accepted quote into an invoice
steps: Open the quote. Accepted ones show Customer accepted.
If they agreed by phone, open the sent quote and tap Approve.
Tap Convert to invoice. The client, items, VAT and CIS come across.
Check it, then tap Send, or Save Draft.

tasks.title: Send an invoice and get paid by card
steps: Open the invoice from the Invoices tab.
Tap Send email. If there is no email on it, type one.
With card payments on, the email carries a Pay now button and the invoice marks itself paid when they pay.

tasks.title: Chase an overdue invoice and mark it paid
steps: Open the Overdue tab. It shows how much is 1 to 30, 31 to 60, 61 to 90 and 90+ days late.
Tap Chase on the invoice. The client is emailed a reminder with a secure payment link. No email on file? You are asked for one.
When the money lands, open the invoice and tap Mark paid.

notes: Overdue: An invoice is overdue the day after its due date if it is not paid. Drafts are never overdue and never chased.
From a job: Opened from a job, this page shows that job’s quotes and invoices only, with a bar to go back to the job.

helps.title: Accounts
helps.what: Profit and loss and a ledger of money in and out for any period. The same figures as Reports and Job financials.
steps: Pick a period: This month, last month, this quarter, this year, the last 12 months or all time.
Read the P&L: Invoiced, less materials, expenses, labour and other job costs, gives gross profit and margin.
Export it: P&L CSV, Ledger CSV or PDF, for your accountant or for Xero, Sage or QuickBooks.

tasks.title: Check this month’s profit
steps: Tap This month in the period row.
Stay on Profit & loss. Read Invoiced, Total costs and Gross profit.
The Cash card shows what was paid in, what is still owed and what is overdue.
tasks.who: Owner and admins. Office managers see a note instead.

tasks.title: See every payment in and out
steps: Pick the period.
Tap Ledger. Paid invoices, purchase orders, expense claims, approved timesheets and job costs are listed as they happened.

tasks.title: Send the figures to your accountant
steps: Pick the period.
Tap P&L CSV, Ledger CSV or PDF. The file downloads.

notes: What counts: Invoiced counts sent, overdue and paid invoices, never drafts. Labour is gross pay from approved timesheets, before PAYE, NI and pension.
Not a payroll package: Elec-Mate is not an accounting or payroll package. Use the exports, or Accounting to send invoices to your books.

helps.title: Tenders
helps.what: Find public sector and commercial work to bid on, and keep every bid you are working on in one pipeline: open, bidding, then won or lost.
steps: Say what you bid for: Tap What we bid for once: where you work, the kind of work and the contract size. Tenders that fit show under Matches for you, on Overview, and in a Monday round-up.

Start a bid: Tap Start bid on a match, or use Discover to search the public tender sources by postcode. Track tender adds one you heard about. Open a tender to copy its pre-qualification answers, filled from your firm records.
Price it: Open the tender and tap AI estimate. Add the drawings and specs and it drafts labour, materials and hazards.
Bid and record the result: Tap Mark submitted when you send it, then Won or Lost. A won tender converts to a job.

tasks.title: Get tenders that fit sent to you
steps: Tap What we bid for.
Add your base postcode and how far you travel, or tick regions.
Pick the work and contract size, tick the accreditations you hold, then tap Save.
Matches show at the top of this page and on Overview. New ones arrive in a Monday notification.

tasks.title: Find tenders near you
steps: Tap Discover.
Type a postcode and tap the search button. Pick 10, 25, 50 or 100 miles.
Tap a result to read it, then Start tender to track it.
Check the details and tap Track tender.

tasks.title: Track a tender you already have
steps: Tap Track tender.
Fill in the tender title and the client (both needed), then the value and submission deadline if you have them.
Tap Track tender to save it to the Open tab.

tasks.title: Get an AI estimate
steps: Open a tender from the Open tab.
Tap AI estimate.
Add the tender documents, then tap Generate estimate.
The estimate appears under AI estimates, in the right-hand column on a computer and under Your bids on a phone.

tasks.title: Record a bid and the result
steps: Open the tender and tap Mark submitted. It moves to Bidding.
When you hear back, open it and tap Won or Lost.
On a won tender, tap Convert to job.

helps.title: Finance
helps.what: Where the money pages live: quotes and invoices, costs, reports and the link to your accounting package. Every figure here matches the page it opens.
steps: Read the top line: Owed to you, overdue, paid in this month and open quotes. Tap one to open the list behind it.
Open a page: Quote, invoice and chase in Quotes & Invoices. Costs in Expenses and Purchase orders.
Check the result: Accounts and Reports show profit for a period. Job financials shows it per job.
notes: Outstanding: The unpaid balance on sent and overdue invoices. Drafts and paid invoices are never counted.

helps.title: Fleet
helps.what: Your vans and cars: who drives them, the daily walk-round check, problems drivers report with photos, and MOT, tax, insurance and service dates.
steps: Add each van and its driver: Tap Add vehicle. Add the registration, the dates you know, and who drives it. The driver then sees it in Worker Tools under My van.
Drivers check it daily: Each morning the driver does the walk-round on their phone. Today shows who has checked and who has not.
Sort problems: A problem comes to your bell with photos. Open the vehicle, get it fixed, then tap Mark fixed. Put it back on the road if it was taken off.
Book what is due: MOT, tax, insurance and service show on your Overview 30 days ahead, and the bell reminds you at 30 days, 7 days and when overdue.

tasks.title: Add a vehicle
steps: Tap Add vehicle.
Type the registration. It is the only required field.
Add make, model, colour, who drives it, and the MOT and tax dates.
Tap Add vehicle at the bottom.

tasks.title: See who has done today’s check
steps: Look at Today near the top.
Vans not checked yet are listed with the driver’s name.
Tap a van to see its checks and any problems.

tasks.title: Deal with a problem a driver reported
steps: Tap the bell notification, or the van under Today.
Look at the photos under Problems.
Once it is fixed, tap Mark fixed. Tick Back on the road if the driver took it off.
tasks.who: The owner and every co-admin, office managers included.

tasks.title: Do a check from the office
steps: Tap the vehicle.
Under Records, tap Daily check.
Enter the mileage, then OK or Problem for each item. A problem needs a photo.
Tap Send check.

tasks.title: Log a service
steps: Tap the vehicle.
Under Records, tap Service history.
Tap Log service, fill it in and tap Save service.

tasks.title: Log fuel
steps: Tap Log fuel.
Pick the vehicle and the date. Both are required.
Add litres, cost, mileage and where you filled up, then tap Log fuel.

tasks.title: Change the driver or status
steps: Tap the vehicle.
Under Quick actions, tap Edit vehicle.
Change who drives it, the status or the dates, then tap Save.

notes: The driver has not joined the app: A driver needs an Elec-Mate account linked to your team to do the check on their phone. Invite them from Team.
Off the road: If a driver says a van is not safe, it is marked Off road and stops nagging for MOT and tax. Put it back from the vehicle once it is fixed.
Who sees what: Drivers see only the van on their name. Photos are private to your firm. Office managers see vehicles and checks but not fuel or service costs.

helps.title: Incidents
helps.what: Every near miss, incident and injury reported on your jobs, in one list. Your team reports from site in Worker Tools or the Site Safety tools; the office can log one here. You see each report, decide on RIDDOR, find the cause, set actions and close it.
steps: Reports arrive on their own: When someone on a job reports a near miss or an injury, you get a bell and it appears under New. Opening it tells them the office has seen it.
Decide on RIDDOR first: For an injury or a dangerous occurrence, record whether the HSE must be told. The page shows the deadline and builds the RIDDOR report for you.
Find the cause and fix it: Write the root cause, then add actions with an owner and a date. Owners on the app are told and can tick them off from site.
Close it with what was done: The person who reported it is sent your close-out summary.

tasks.title: Log a report from the office
steps: Tap Report incident.
Pick what kind it was. Choose Injury if anyone was hurt: it goes in the accident book.
Say what happened, where and when, and add photos.
Tap Log report.

tasks.title: Work through a report from the team
steps: Tap the report under New.
Record the RIDDOR decision if it is an injury.
Write the root cause and add actions with owners.
Countersign it to show the firm has checked it.
Write what was done and tap Close report.
tasks.who: A report your team made stays theirs. You add the follow-up and countersign it; you cannot change what they wrote.

notes: Where reports are kept: Incidents are Site Safety records: near misses in the near-miss register, injuries in the accident book. The same records open from Site Safety in this hub and in the Electrical Hub.
Who sees them: Only the firm’s owner and managers. Crew never see incident reports, because they name the injured person. A worker sees their own reports and what the office did.

helps.title: Site diary
helps.what: One diary per job. The office writes a daily log, the team adds notes and photos from site, and both land here in date order, with who clocked in each day.
steps: The team writes from site: Each note your team adds in Worker Tools, Progress notes, lands here with its photos. You get a bell when one comes in.
Add the office log: Tap Write a log for the day: work done, weather, materials and photos.
Find anything later: Search every word, filter by person or job, and pick Today, This week, This month or All.

tasks.title: Write a daily log
steps: Tap Write a log.
Pick the job and the date.
Say what was done. Add finished items, materials and photos if you have them.
Leave Share with the client off unless the client should see it.
Tap Save to the diary.

tasks.title: Read what the team sent
steps: Tap From the team to see only their notes.
Tap a note to read it in full and see its photos.
Tap a photo to open it full screen. Swipe for the next one.

tasks.title: Share an entry with the client
steps: Tap the entry to open it.
Turn on Share with the client. It can then show on the client portal.
Turn it off again to keep it to your team.

tasks.title: Sign off a daily log
steps: Open a daily log that says Daily log.
Read it over, then tap Sign off log at the bottom.

notes: Every number matches the list: Entries, From the team, Photos and Shared count the same range as the list under them.
Settling a dispute: Search a word like socket or the client name. Every entry is dated, with who wrote it and the photos taken that day.

helps.title: Issues
helps.what: Everything raised on a job in one list: snags, defects, variations, questions for the client and delays. Each job has a punch list the client signs off at handover.
steps: Raise it: Tap Report issue, or let the team raise snags from site with photos.
Work the punch list: Open a job's Punch list, tick each snag off as it is fixed, and add new ones as you walk round.
Get it signed: Tap Get the client to sign it off. Variations get a price and go to the client to approve.

tasks.title: Report an issue
steps: Tap Report issue.
Pick the job, then what it is: Snag, Defect, Variation, Question (RFI), Delay or Other.
Give it a title, how serious it is and where on site.
Add who is on it, a due date and photos if you have them.
Tap Report issue at the bottom.

tasks.title: Work through a punch list and get it signed off
steps: On the job's card, tap Punch list.
