Tap the circle next to a snag when it is fixed. Tap it again to reopen it.
Type a new snag in the box at the bottom and tap Add.
When it is done, tap Get the client to sign it off. Add their name and email, or make a link to send yourself.

tasks.title: Turn a variation into a variation order
steps: Open the Variations tab and tap the variation.
Put in the price change and what the extra work is.
Tap Raise variation order. It goes into Job financials as Pending.
Tap Send to the client to approve. When they sign, tap Add to the job value.

tasks.title: Move an issue on and resolve it
steps: Tap the issue.
Under Where it is up to, pick In progress when work starts.
When it is fixed, tap Resolve issue, say how, then Mark as resolved.

notes: Where did Quality & Snags go?: It was the same list filtered to snags. Old links now open here on the Snags & defects tab.
Still open, Resolved, Everything: The chips under the tabs pick which issues show. Still open is the default.

helps.title: Testing
helps.what: The certificates raised on each job, read straight from the certificate. Every reading is checked against the certificate’s own BS 7671 limits, so anything out of limit shows here without anyone retyping it.
steps: Your electrician tests as normal: They fill in the schedule of tests on the EICR, EIC or Minor Works in the Electrical Hub.
Link it to the job: Tap Link a certificate, pick the job and the certificate. Best matches come first.
Check the results: Each card shows circuits tested, anything out of limit and where the QS sign-off is.

tasks.title: Link a certificate to a job
steps: Tap Link a certificate. From a job sheet, tap Certificates first and the job is already chosen.
Pick the job if it asks.
Find the certificate. Ones whose address or client match the job show Best match.
Tap Link. Its results show on the job straight away.

tasks.title: Find readings that are out of limit
steps: Tap Needs attention.
Tap a certificate. Circuits to look at come first.
Each circuit shows its readings, which check failed, and any test not recorded.

tasks.title: Check the instrument
steps: Open a certificate.
Look at Instrument. If the serial matches your kit register, it shows the calibration date and says if it is overdue.

notes: Where the old test log went: The hand-typed test list has gone. Results now come from the certificate itself, so there is one record, not two.
What the colours mean: Red is a reading outside its limit. Amber is a circuit with a core test not recorded yet. Green is a circuit within limits.

helps.title: QS reviews
helps.what: Certificates your team sends for Qualifying Supervisor sign-off. Countersign each one, or send it back with reasons. The reasons are counted so you can see which mistakes keep coming back.
steps: Open what is waiting: Waiting lists the EICRs, EICs and Minor Works sent for sign-off, oldest first. Tap one to open it.
Check it: Read the summary, observations and test schedule, or tap View PDF. Add a comment against anything wrong.
Decide: Approve & countersign, or Return with reasons. The electrician is told why straight away.

tasks.title: Approve and countersign a certificate
steps: On Waiting, tap the certificate.
Check the details. Tap View PDF to see the certificate itself.
Tap Approve & countersign.
Check your name, sign in the box and add a comment if you like.
Tap Confirm approval. Your countersignature goes on the PDF.
tasks.who: The owner, an admin manager or a team member with the QS role. Office managers can look but not sign.

tasks.title: Send a certificate back with reasons
steps: Open the certificate.
Tap + Comment next to a circuit or observation to point at the exact problem.
Tap Return with reasons and tick what is wrong, for example Missing test readings or Zs over the limit.
Add a note if it helps, then tap Return certificate.

tasks.title: See the mistakes that keep coming back
steps: Look at Common returns, under the numbers.
It counts the reasons ticked over the last 20 decisions, for example Missing test readings 4 of the last 20.
Use it to coach the team on the one thing that keeps going wrong.

tasks.title: Fix it yourself
steps: Open the certificate.
Tap Edit cert. It opens in the normal certificate form, ready to change.

tasks.title: Print the review register
steps: Tap Export register at the top. It opens a printable record of every sign-off for an assessor.

notes: A QS who is not the owner: A team member with the QS role signs from Worker Tools, QS reviews, To review. The bell tells them when something is sent.
Team certificates: The owner and the principal QS also get a Team certificates tab: every certificate the team has made, to open and edit.
Nothing coming in?: Give someone the QS role in Team. Certificates only arrive here once the team sends them for sign-off.

helps.title: Photo gallery
helps.what: Every photo from every job in one place: what the office uploads, and what the team takes on snags, progress notes and tasks.
steps: They arrive by themselves: A photo on a snag, a progress note or a task lands here with who took it and when.
Find the one you want: See photos by job or by day, and pick where they came from: Uploaded, Snags, Issues, Site diary or Tasks.
Use it: Open a photo to mark it up, share it with the client, download it or jump to the snag it belongs to.

tasks.title: Upload a photo
steps: Tap Upload.
Tap to select a photo, then pick Before, During, After, Completion or Issue.
Pick the job. Tap Add current location to put it on the map.
Tap Upload photo.

tasks.title: See only the team's snag photos
steps: Tap Snags in the row under the search.
Tap a photo, then Open the snag to see the issue it belongs to.

tasks.title: Mark up a photo
steps: Open the photo.
Tap Mark up. Draw with the pen, or use an arrow, box or ring, in red, yellow, white or blue.
Tap Save as a new photo. The original stays as it was; the copy is filed on the same job.

tasks.title: Approve a photo and share it with the client
steps: Open a photo you uploaded (Uploaded in the row of sources).
Tap Approve. A green tick shows on it.
Tap Share with client. A blue eye shows on it.

tasks.title: Compare before and after
steps: Upload a Before and an After or Completion photo on the same job.
Tap Before & after, then tap the pair.

notes: Photo unavailable: Shown only when the file really is missing. Ask whoever took it to add it again.
Approve and share: Only photos uploaded here can be approved or shared one by one. Diary photos are shared with their diary entry.

helps.title: The kit register
helps.what: Every company tool and tester, who has it (a person or a van), when its PAT test or calibration is due, and what each van carries.
steps: Add the kit: Testers, drills, ladders, anything the firm owns. Add the serial number and barcode for testers.
Issue it: Give each item to a person or put it on a van. They confirm they have it in Worker Tools, so you always know who has the Megger.
Log each test: Record each PAT test or calibration. The next due date updates itself and the holder is reminded before it runs out.
Stock the vans: In Van stock, put the materials each van carries. The driver logs what they use on a job, and a draft order is made when it runs low.

tasks.title: Add kit to the register
steps: Tap Add kit.
Type the equipment name and pick the category. Both are required.
Add the status, serial number, barcode and purchase details.
Add the last PAT and calibration dates and when they are next due.
Tap Add equipment.

tasks.title: Issue kit to a person or a van
steps: Tap the item.
Under Who has it, tap Issue (or Move to someone else).
Pick A person or A van, then tap who.
Add a note if it helps, then tap Issue.

tasks.title: Take kit back into the office
steps: Tap the item.
Under Who has it, tap Back in the office.

tasks.title: Deal with a fault or lost report
steps: Open the notification, or tap Faulty or lost above the list.
Tap the item. The report, who sent it and the photo are at the top.
Once it is fixed or found, tap Fixed, back in use (or Found it).

tasks.title: Log a PAT test or calibration
steps: Tap the item.
Under Log a test, pick PAT test or Calibration, then Passed or Failed.
Set the date tested and when it is next due (12 months on by default).
For a calibration, add the certificate number.
Tap Log PAT test or Log calibration.

tasks.title: Find kit by scanning it
steps: Tap the barcode button in the search box.
Point the camera at the barcode or serial label.
The item opens if it is on the register.

tasks.title: Stock a van
steps: Tap Van stock at the top, then the van.
Tap Add item and search your price book.
Enter how many are on the van, the level to reorder at and the level to fill back up to.
Pick the usual supplier if the price book does not say, and scan the barcode on the box.
Tap Add to van.

tasks.title: See what came off a van onto a job
steps: Tap Van stock, then the van.
Recent activity lists what was used, on which job and by whom.

notes: Why calibration matters: A tester out of calibration undermines every certificate it was used on. Keep the certificate number with each calibration.
Reminders: You get a reminder 30 days before a PAT test or calibration is due. Whoever holds the item gets one 14 days before, on the day, and if it runs out.
Money: Workers and office managers never see buy prices or what the kit cost. Van stock shows quantities only.

helps.title: Jobs
helps.what: Every job the firm is running, with who is on it and where it is up to. Open a job to book people, change its status or get directions.
steps: Add the job: Tap New job. Three short steps: the job, the site and dates, then the scope.
Put people on it: Open the job and tap Assign. Pick the people, set the dates, and they get a push.
Keep the status right: Tap Edit job to move it between Active, Pending, On hold, Completed or Cancelled.

tasks.title: Add a new job
steps: Tap New job.
Job: type the job title and the client, and pick a status.
Site & dates: type the site address (used for directions and the live map), then the start and end dates.
Scope: say what is being done. Add the job value and people needed if you know them.
Tap Create job. It opens straight away so you can book people.

tasks.title: Put people on a job
steps: Tap the job in the list to open it.
Under Assigned workers, tap Assign.
Tick the people. Anyone already booked elsewhere on those dates shows a clash warning.
Tap Continue to assignment, check the dates and notes, then tap Assign.

tasks.title: Change a job’s status
steps: Open the job.
Tap Edit job.
Under Status & value, pick the new status.
Tap Save changes. The change is written to the job’s activity.

tasks.title: Find a job
steps: Use the tabs: All, Active, Pending, On hold, Completed.
Search by title, client or location.
The filter button narrows by status and job value.

notes: Who sees money: Job values only show for people allowed to see the firm’s money. Office managers see the jobs without the value.
Flags on a job: Red and amber pills on a row mean an incident, an overdue invoice, a certificate running out or money still due.

helps.title: The diary
helps.what: Who is where this week. Book people onto jobs, move bookings, and the team gets one push with their changes.
steps: See the week: On a computer, days run across and people down. On a phone, tap a day in the strip to see it.
Book or move: Tap a job, a person or a booking. Pick who, when and how long, then tap Book or Save.
The team is told: Each person gets one push about a minute after your last change, or tap Send now.

tasks.title: Book someone on a job
steps: Phone: tap the day in the strip, then tap Book next to the person, or tap a job under Nobody booked.
Computer: hover the person’s day and click the plus, or click a job in the Nobody booked row.
Pick the job if it asks. Who: pick the person. When: pick the start day. Time on site: Full day, 2h, 4h or 6h.
Tap Book.

tasks.title: Drag a job onto someone (computer)
steps: Find the job in the Nobody booked row, or under To schedule.
Drag it onto the person and the day.
If it clashes with another job or their leave, you get a warning with an Undo.

tasks.title: Move a booking
steps: Phone: tap the day, then tap the booking under the person.
Computer: drag the booking to another day or person, or click it.
Change Who to give it to someone else, or pick a new day under When, then tap Save.
To take them off the job, tap Take off, then Yes, take off.

tasks.title: Copy last week
steps: Go to the week you are planning.
Tap Copy last week.
Check the list: anyone still on a job at the end of last week stays on it to Friday. Finished, cancelled and on-hold jobs are left alone.
Tap Copy … bookings.

tasks.title: Send the changes now
steps: After a change, a bar shows how many changes are not sent yet.
Tap Send now to push them straight away instead of waiting a minute.

notes: Red means a clash: A person shows red when they are double-booked, booked over a working day, or booked on leave.
Same dates everywhere: The Timeline and the Job board read the same bookings, so a move here shows there too.

helps.title: The job board
helps.what: Every job from enquiry to complete, as cards in columns. Move a card when the job moves on.
steps: Read the columns: Enquiry, Quoted, Confirmed, Scheduled, In progress, Testing, Complete and On hold.
Move a card: On a computer, drag it. On a phone, press and hold it, then tap the new stage.
Open a job: Tap a card to open the job, book people and change the details.

tasks.title: Move a job to the next stage
steps: Computer: drag the card into the new column, or right-click it and pick Move to….
Phone: swipe to the column, press and hold the card, then tap the stage.

tasks.title: Add a job straight onto the board
steps: Tap Add job at the bottom of the column.
Computer: type the job title and client, then tap Add job.
Phone: type the title and tap Add. The client and site show TBC until you fill them in.

tasks.title: Start from a template
steps: Tap Templates.
Pick one and tap Use.
To make one, right-click a card on a computer and pick Save as template.

tasks.title: Archive a finished job
steps: Computer: right-click the card and pick Archive.
Phone: press and hold the card and tap Archive Job.
Tap Archived at the top to find it again.

notes: Filters: Use Filters to hide completed jobs, and the two view buttons to switch between the board and a list.

helps.title: The timeline
helps.what: Every booked job as a bar across the week, month or quarter. Change a job’s dates here and everyone on it moves too.
steps: Pick a range: Week, Month or Quarter. Use Prev, Today and Next to step through.
Change the dates: On a computer, drag a bar or its right edge. On a phone, tap the job.
The crew moves too: Everyone booked slides with the job and gets one push about it.

tasks.title: Move a job or change its dates
steps: Phone: tap the job in the list. Use −1 wk, −1 day, +1 day or +1 wk, or set Starts and Ends, then tap Save dates.
Computer: drag the bar left or right to move it, or drag its right edge to make it run longer or shorter.
Computer, by keyboard: select the bar, press Enter and set the dates in the sheet.

tasks.title: Spot jobs running late
steps: Running late in the stats counts jobs past their end date that are not complete or on hold.
On a phone those jobs say Running late in orange.

notes: Team availability: The list under the chart shows who is on leave, so you can see who is free before you move a job.

helps.title: Worker tracking
helps.what: Where the team is right now: on site, travelling, in the office or off. It comes from the status each worker sets on their phone.
steps: Workers set a status: In Worker Tools, Status. On site and En route need their location on.
See it here: The map and the list update as they change. A status older than 12 hours drops to Off duty.
Act on it: Call, message, or check someone out who forgot to.

tasks.title: Check someone in to a job
steps: Tap the check in button (the person with a plus).
Pick the worker and the job site.
Tap Check in to site.

tasks.title: Message or call a worker
steps: Find them in the Workers list.
Tap the phone to call, or the message button to write to them.
A message lands in their Worker Tools comms with a push.

tasks.title: Check out someone who forgot
steps: Find them in the list.
Tap Check out. Their shift ends.

notes: Phone view: On a phone, use the list and map buttons at the top to switch views.

helps.title: Job packs
helps.what: One pack per job with the scope, documents, certificates and briefing. Send it to the crew and see who has signed.
steps: Make a pack: Tap New pack, or tap a job under Jobs awaiting pack.
Get the documents ready: The RAMS, method statement and briefing pack are made in the pack’s Docs tab.
Send it and chase: Send tab, Send to workers. Each person signs on their phone. The pack turns Complete by itself when the last person signs.

tasks.title: Make a pack for a job
steps: Tap New pack, or tap the job under Jobs awaiting pack so it is already picked.
Work through Start, Details, Hazards, Team and Review.
Tap Create pack.

tasks.title: Send a pack to the crew
steps: Tap the pack to open it.
Make sure Docs shows all three documents made and at least one worker is assigned.
Open the Send tab and tap Send to workers.

tasks.title: See who has signed and chase
steps: Open the pack and tap Send.
Each person shows when they signed, or a Chase button.
Tap Chase for one person, or Chase everyone still to sign. On the list, Chase does the same in one tap.

notes: The documents themselves: Making and checking the RAMS, method statement and briefing is covered in the Safety help.
The tabs: Draft has not gone out. Sent is with the crew and shows how many have signed. Complete means everyone has signed it off; nobody sets it by hand.
Certificates: The certificates a pack needs are checked against each person’s Elec-ID on the start date. A red line on the list names who is missing what.
Site safety PDF: Site safety PDF, at the top or inside a pack, builds the one-page summary a principal contractor asks for from the job’s crew, RAMS, sign-offs and compliance documents.

helps.title: The jobs hub
helps.what: Everything about running jobs, one tap away. The numbers at the top open the page behind them.
steps: Plan: Jobs, Job board, Diary and Timeline: what is on and who is on it.
On site: Worker tracking, Progress logs, Issues, Testing and Quality.
Kit and money: Fleet, Kit register, Photos, Purchase orders and Job financials.

helps.title: People
helps.what: Everything about your team in one place: who is on it, their cards and tickets, hours, leave, messages, and hiring.
steps: Start with Needs you: Needs you lists what is waiting today: cards expired, hours to approve, leave to decide, applications, people who never joined.
Open a page: Your team (Team, Credentials, Timesheets, Leave, Communications, Subcontractors, Contracts) runs the day. Grow the team holds Job vacancies, Talent pool and Apprentice progress.
Watch Cards in date: Cards in date is the share of your active team with an ECS card in date. Tap it to open Credentials.
notes: What each page is for: Team: add people and chase invites. Credentials: Elec-IDs, ECS checks and renewals. Timesheets: approve hours. Leave: holiday and allowances. Communications: messages with read receipts. Talent Pool, Job Vacancies and Apprentice Progress: hiring and training.

helps.title: Team
helps.what: Everyone on your books. Add people, get them signed in to the app, and keep their details right. Someone only works in the app for your firm once they have joined.
steps: Add someone: Tap Add team member. With an email address, they get an invite to join straight away.
Chase who has not joined: The Invited tab lists people who never signed in. Send a reminder, up to three, a day apart.
Keep details right: Tap a person to call, message or assign them. Edit profile changes their role, pay and status.

tasks.title: Add someone and send the invite
steps: Tap Add team member.
Who: full name and email (the email is what sends the invite). Tap Next.
Role and pay: job role, team role and pay. Tap Next.
Check the review, then tap Add team member.

tasks.title: Chase someone who has not joined
steps: Open the Invited tab.
Tap Send reminder under their name. It sends a fresh invite email.
If it says Chase in a few hours, the last one went less than a day ago. After three reminders it says Chased 3 times.
Lost the email? Tap Team code and share the code in your WhatsApp group or by text.

tasks.title: Change someone’s details
steps: Tap the person in the list.
Tap Edit profile at the bottom.
Change their role, contact details, pay or status.
Tap Save changes.
tasks.who: Owner, admins and office managers. Office managers never see pay.

tasks.title: Remove someone from the team
steps: Tap the person, then Edit profile.
Tap the bin button at the bottom.
Tap Remove to confirm.

tasks.title: Message or assign several people
steps: Tap the tick box button next to Add team member.
Tick the people you want, or Select all.
Tap Message to send them one message, or Assign to put them on a job.

notes: Seats: Each linked team member uses a seat on your plan. They pay nothing themselves.

helps.title: Credentials
helps.what: Each person’s Elec-ID: their ECS card, tickets and training, how you checked them, and what is running out. The competence matrix is the grid you send to a principal contractor.
steps: Give everyone an Elec-ID: Add credential lists the people without one. Tap a person, or Create all.
Record your checks: Open a person and tap their ECS card to record that you saw it or checked it on the card checker.
Stay ahead of renewals: The Expiring and Expired tabs show who needs a renewal. Nudge to renew sends them a message.

tasks.title: Give someone an Elec-ID
steps: Tap Add credential. It lists the people with no Elec-ID.
Tap the person, or tap Create all to make empty ones for everyone.
Add their ECS card type, card number and expiry, then tap Create Elec-ID.

tasks.title: Record that you checked an ECS card
steps: Tap the person in the list.
Under Checks, tap ECS card.
Pick Document seen or Verified at source, and say how you checked it (for example on the JIB/ECS card checker).
Tap Save. Your name and the date go on the record.

tasks.title: Add a training record or ticket
steps: Open the person.
Tap Add training.
Fill in the course name, completion date and expiry if it has one.
Tap Add Training Record.

tasks.title: Chase a renewal
steps: Open the Expiring or Expired tab.
Tap the person.
Under Needs renewing, tap Nudge to renew.

tasks.title: Send the competence matrix to a principal contractor
steps: Tap Competence matrix.
Set the site requirements if they asked for particular cards.
Tap Export PDF, Share, or CSV.

tasks.title: Check someone’s Elec-ID on site
steps: Tap Scan.
Type their Elec-ID number (like EM-7K3P4N), or tap Scan QR code with camera.
You see their card, training and whether anything has run out.

helps.title: Talent pool
helps.what: Electricians who have switched on “Let firms find me” in their Elec-ID. You see first name, area and credentials. Phone and email stay private, so you contact them through messages.
steps: Narrow it down: Use the chips (Verified+, EV Charging, Solar PV, Senior 8+ yrs), the search, or Filters.
Shortlist: Tap the bookmark to save someone. Everyone managing the firm sees the shortlist.
Get in touch: Message them, or Invite them to apply for one of your live vacancies.

tasks.title: Find the right person
steps: Tap a chip at the top, or type a name, skill or area in the search.
Tap Filters for tier, specialisms, experience and day rate, then tap Done.
Tap someone’s photo to see their full profile.

tasks.title: Message someone
steps: Tap Message under their name.
Write your message.
Tap Send Message.

tasks.title: Invite someone to apply
steps: Tap Invite under their name.
Pick one of your live vacancies.
Add a personal message if you like, then tap Send Invitation.

tasks.title: Shortlist someone
steps: Tap the bookmark on the right of their card.
Tap it again to take them off.

helps.title: Apprentices
helps.what: Live college progress for the apprentices on your team: off-the-job hours, end-point assessment and progress reviews. Hours they log at work wait here for you to attest.
steps: Attest their hours: Awaiting your attestation lists training hours they logged at work. Open one and attest it, or send it back.
Check progress: Tap an apprentice for their off-the-job hours, EPA dates and reviews.
Keep reviews on time: Add your view before a review and sign the summary after. Chase an overdue one in one tap.
Bring in the ones not on your team: Not on your team yet lists apprentices whose college names your firm but who are not on your team. Ask them to arrange a review, or add them to your team.

tasks.title: Attest training hours
steps: Under Awaiting your attestation, tap the entry.
Read what they logged and open any evidence.
Tap Attest (it shows the hours).
tasks.who: The office here. Supervisors, project managers and apprentice co-ordinators can also confirm hours from Worker Tools.

tasks.title: Send hours back
steps: Open the entry.
Tap Send back.
Write what needs changing. The apprentice sees it.
Tap Confirm send back.

tasks.title: Check an apprentice’s progress
steps: Under Your apprentices, tap the person.
See off-the-job hours against what is needed, EPA dates and progress reviews.

tasks.title: Chase an overdue review
steps: Open the apprentice. Overdue reviews show a red Review due.
Tap Ask to arrange review.

tasks.title: Apprentices not on your team yet
steps: Open the Not on your team yet card. It lists apprentices whose college names your firm as their employer.
Tap a person.
Tap Ask to arrange review. It works without them being on your team, once every 3 days.
Or tap Add them to your team. They get an invite by email and link their own account when they accept it.
tasks.who: The owner, admins and office managers.

tasks.title: Take part in a progress review
steps: Open the apprentice.
Tap Add your view before the review, or Read and sign the review summary after it.

notes: When you are told: The moment an apprentice logs hours, the owner, admins and their named supervisor get a bell and a push that opens the entry. Each person is told once. If hours wait 3 days or more, you get a reminder on Monday.

helps.title: Subcontractors
helps.what: Labour-only sparkies and regular subbies on your books. They get the same jobs, packs, briefings and timesheets as your team, with no holiday or PAYE payroll. You pay them by a self-bill statement from the days you approved, with CIS worked out for you.
steps: Pick the tax month: CIS runs from the 6th to the 5th. The page opens on this tax month; use the arrows for the one before.
Check days and cover: Each subbie shows the days you approved, days still waiting, and whether their insurance and ECS card are in date.
Issue the statement: The owner or an admin issues a self-bill statement. CIS comes off labour only; materials are never taxed.

tasks.title: Set up a subbie
steps: Add them from Team with the Subcontractor type, or change an existing person to Subcontractor.
Here, tap the subbie, then Edit.
Fill in trade and public liability insurance (provider, policy, cover, expiry).
Owner or admin: set the day or hourly rate, CIS status, UTR and HMRC verification number.
Tap Save.
tasks.who: Office managers can set trade and insurance. Only the owner and admins see or set rates, CIS and UTR.

tasks.title: Issue a self-bill statement
steps: Check the tax month at the top.
Tap the subbie. Approved days, other costs and materials are listed.
Tap Issue statement and check the sums: days times rate is labour, CIS comes off labour and other costs, materials are paid in full.
Tap Issue. They get the statement in their app.

tasks.title: Export statements for your accountant
steps: Pick the tax month.
Tap Export statements. You get a CSV of every statement in the month.

notes: How CIS is worked out: Labour (days times day rate, or hours times hourly rate) plus other costs such as travel are liable to deduction. Materials are not. Gross 0%, verified 20%, higher rate or not verified 30%. Pennies are rounded down, in the subbie’s favour.
Who sees what: Office managers see days, trade and insurance, never rates, CIS, UTR or amounts. Subbies see their own statements in Worker Tools, My pay.
No holiday, no PAYE: Subbies have no holiday allowance and are left out of the payroll run. They pay their own tax through Self Assessment.

helps.title: Job vacancies
helps.what: Post jobs, take applications and move people from new applicant to hired. Hiring someone puts them straight on your team.
steps: Post a vacancy: Post vacancy walks you through the basics, pay, requirements and a review.
Work the candidates: The Candidates tab moves each person along: Shortlist, Interview, Make offer, Hire.
Invite the talent pool: When a vacancy goes live, invite the matching electricians who opted in to be found. They apply with their Elec-ID.
Talk to them: Messages holds your conversations with applicants and people from the talent pool.

tasks.title: Post a vacancy
steps: Tap Post vacancy.
Fill in Job Basics, Compensation and Requirements, tapping Continue each time.
Check the Review and tap Publish vacancy.
Not ready? Tap Save draft. It waits in the Draft tab.

tasks.title: Publish, pause or reopen a vacancy
steps: On the Vacancies tab pick Live, Draft or Closed.
Tap the vacancy.
Tap Publish for a draft, Pause for a live one, or Reopen.

tasks.title: Move a candidate to hired
steps: Open the Candidates tab.
Tap Shortlist on a new applicant.
Tap Interview… and book the time. They are told the interview is booked.
After the interview tap Make offer and enter the pay, start date and role.
Tap Hire. Add their date of birth if you have it.

tasks.title: Invite the talent pool
steps: Publish a vacancy. The talent pool sheet opens straight away.
It lists the available electricians who match the role. Everyone is ticked.
Untick anyone you do not want, add a message if you like, and tap Invite.
Later, open a live vacancy and tap Invite matching electricians to invite more.
tasks.who: Owner, admins and office managers on the Employer plan.

tasks.title: Turn a candidate down
steps: Tap the candidate.
Tap Reject and give a reason. It is kept in your private notes.
Changed your mind? Open them and tap Reinstate to New.

tasks.title: Message applicants
steps: Open the Messages tab.
Tap a conversation to reply.

notes: Who is in the talent pool: Only electricians who switched on Let firms find me in their Elec-ID. You see their first name and initial, card, area and declared rate. Never their phone or email.

What the numbers mean: New candidates are applications nobody has looked at yet. In progress is shortlisted, interviewed and offered. Hired counts people hired in the last 30 days. The Talent pool panel shows who you invited and how many applied.

helps.title: Contracts
helps.what: Employment and subcontractor contracts, sent from the person and signed on their phone. Your customer terms live here too.
steps: Send from the person: Open someone in Team and tap Send contract, or tap Send a contract here and pick them.
They sign on their phone: They get an email with a link and, if they use Worker Tools, it waits in Sign-offs. They keep a signed copy.
You countersign: Once they have signed, open the contract here and tap Sign as employer. It turns Active.
Customer terms: The Customer terms tab holds the terms that print on every quote and that customers agree to on the accept page.

tasks.title: Send a contract to someone
steps: Tap Send a contract, or open the person in Team and tap Send contract.
Pick the template: employment, subcontractor or a letter.
Check the start date and pay, and fill anything else you know.
Tap Send for signature.
tasks.who: Owner and admins. Contracts carry pay, so office managers only see the status.

tasks.title: Countersign a signed contract
steps: Open the contract from Your contracts.
Tap Sign as employer, draw your signature and save.

tasks.title: Change your customer terms
steps: Open the Customer terms tab.
Tap Edit terms, tick what applies, add your own.
Tap Save.

notes: Who sees contracts: The owner and admins. Office managers see whether a person has signed, never the contract or the pay.

helps.title: Recurring work
helps.what: Work that comes round again: maintenance visits, PAT rounds, emergency lighting tests, and the re-test date on every certificate. Elec-Mate books the next visit for you, so nothing lives on a spreadsheet.
steps: Make a job recurring: Open any job and tap Make this recurring. Pick how often and when the next visit is.
The next visit books itself: Before each visit is due, a new job is put in the diary for that date, with the same crew if you asked. You get a bell.

Renewals come from certificates: Every certificate with a re-test date (EICR, EIC, emergency lighting, fire alarm and more) that the firm issues, or signs off in QS review, shows here when it is due. Book it as a job in one tap.

tasks.title: Make a job recurring
steps: Open the job (Jobs, then tap it).
Tap Make this recurring.
Pick how often: every 3 months, every year, and so on.
Set the date of the next visit and how many days ahead to book it.
Leave Same crew next time on to send the same people.
Tap Make it recurring.
tasks.who: Owner, admins and office managers. Only the owner and admins set a price or draft invoices.

tasks.title: Book a certificate renewal
steps: Open the Renewals tab.
Find the certificate. Overdue ones are at the top.
Tap Book as a job to put the re-test in the diary, or Book and repeat to keep it coming at the same interval.

tasks.title: Pause or stop a repeat visit
steps: Open Repeat visits.
Tap the visit.
Tap Pause, Resume or End.

notes: What the crew sees: On each repeat visit, Worker Tools shows a Last visit card: who went, their notes, and the snags they found.
Which certificates count: Certificates issued on the firm account, and any a team member sent through your QS review and you approved.

helps.title: The safety hub
helps.what: Everything that proves your sites are safe, one tap away. The line under the title says what needs doing first, and the figures open the page behind them.
steps: Before work starts: Job packs, Checklists and Site Safety: the RAMS, briefing and checks your crew signs before anyone starts.
When something happens: Incidents and Safety alerts: log accidents and near misses, follow them up and close them out.
Keep the paperwork in date: Policies, Contracts, Training records and Compliance, each with what has expired or is due soon.
notes: What the colours mean: Red is a problem, such as an open incident or something expired. Yellow needs doing now, such as RAMS to sign off. Everything else is white.

helps.title: Safety documents
helps.what: One run gives a job its RAMS and its method statement, filled in with your company, the supervisor and a first-aider from your team. Every run is saved to the job.
steps: Pick the job: The site, client and dates come from the job. Contractor, supervisor, first-aider and site contact come from your team and their certificates.
Generate: Tap Generate, check the details and the description, then generate. If the same brief was run for this job before, you are offered that one instead of running it again.
Check and issue: Open the run, check every hazard and step, then issue the PDF. It goes into the job pack for the crew to sign.

tasks.title: Make the safety documents for a job
steps: Pick the job under The job.
Check Filled in for you. Fix anything missing in Team or Settings, or change it on the next screen.
Tap Generate.
When it is ready, check it and download the full RAMS to issue it.

notes: Where a first-aider comes from: Someone on the job’s crew with an in-date first aid certificate on their record. With nobody, the field is left for you to fill in.
Writing one yourself: Write by hand opens the method statement builder. A RAMS typed in RAMS is on the same register.

helps.title: RAMS register
helps.what: Every RAMS the firm has, in one list: written by hand, generated with AI, or attached to a job pack. Each with its job, status and a PDF.
steps: Find one: Filter by job or status, or search by name, site or assessor.
Open it: Read the hazards, change the status, countersign a worker’s RAMS, or download the PDF.
Bring older ones in: RAMS you wrote before the firm had a register are still your own. Move to firm files them here. Move back undoes it.
notes: What is never moved: Only RAMS you made yourself can be moved, and only when you ask. A worker’s own RAMS stay theirs; one they file against a firm job shows here to read and countersign.
Not issued: An AI run that has not been issued yet. Open it to check and issue the PDF.

helps.title: AI quote
helps.what: A first-draft quote in a couple of minutes. Pick a job, or describe the work, and the AI lists the materials and labour. Prices come from your own price book wherever it has the item; anything else is marked as an estimate for you to check.
steps: Pick the job: Choose an open job or describe the work. Give it a job type so it can compare with your past jobs.
Check the draft: Every line says where its price came from: your price book, your rate, or an AI estimate to check.
Send from the quote builder: Save it as a draft on the job, adjust anything, then send it to the customer as normal.

tasks.title: Draft a quote from a job
steps: Tap Start a draft.
Pick From a job and choose the job, or Describe the work and type what needs doing. Add a job type if you can.
Tap Draft my quote. It takes 20 to 40 seconds; keep the sheet open.

tasks.title: Check the draft and save it
steps: Read Where the prices came from: price book, your rate, or an AI estimate to check.
Edit the scope of works (the customer sees it). Under Labour, tap Use … hours to match your past jobs if it shows.
Tap Save draft and review. It opens in the quote builder as a draft on the job.

tasks.title: Finish an earlier draft
steps: Under Recent AI drafts, tap one marked Check.
It opens in the quote builder. Change anything, then send it as normal.

notes: Labour hours: When you have finished jobs of the same type with approved timesheets, the draft shows how long they really took and lets you use that figure.
VAT and CIS: Follow your firm settings: not VAT registered means no VAT, and reverse charge and CIS apply where you have them switched on.
Who sees what: Office managers can draft quotes. They see sell prices only, never buy prices or markup.
Cost: Drafting the same job again with the same prices reuses the earlier draft rather than running the AI again.

helps.title: Accounting
helps.what: Your firm's Xero, QuickBooks or Sage connection in one place. Invoices go across to your books by themselves, and at the end of each pay period one tap sends approved hours, expenses and mileage to payroll, with holiday, sick pay and the minimum wage checked.
steps: Connect once: The owner or an admin connects the firm’s accounting package. It is the same connection the Electrical Hub uses, so there is only ever one.
Invoices sync by themselves: When an invoice is emailed it goes to your package. If one fails, it says why on the invoice, with Sync now to try again.

Send to payroll: Pick the pay period and your payroll software, then tap Check and send. You see the minimum wage check, holiday and sick pay for each person, then get the file. Everyone’s hours are marked as sent so nothing goes twice.
Workers can see it: Each worker’s Timesheet and My pay pages say when their hours went to payroll, so nobody has to ask.

tasks.title: Connect Xero, QuickBooks or Sage
steps: Under Connection, tap Xero, QuickBooks or Sage.
Sign in on the package’s own page and allow access. Elec-Mate never sees your password.
You come back here with a note saying it is connected.
Leave Send invoices to … when they are emailed switched on so each invoice goes across by itself.
tasks.who: Owner and admins. Others see Ask the owner or an admin to connect it.

tasks.title: Get an invoice into your books
steps: Invoices go across when they are emailed, if the switch is on.
Under Invoices, any that failed or are waiting show Sync now or Try again, with the reason.
Tap Sync now on one, or Sync … now at the top for all of them.
tasks.who: Owner and admins. Office managers see the counts only.

tasks.title: Run payroll for the pay period
steps: Approve the period’s timesheets first. Only approved hours go.
Under Send to payroll, pick Last period or This period (calendar months until a pay period is set).
Pick your payroll software: BrightPay, QuickBooks, Sage, Moneysoft, Xero or Other. Switch expenses and mileage on or off.
Tap Check and send. Read the minimum wage and holiday checks, then tap Send and save the file.
tasks.who: Owner and admins get pay, expenses and mileage. Office managers get an hours-only file.

tasks.title: Set the pay period
steps: Under Send to payroll, tap Set pay period (or Change pay period).
Choose how often you pay, when the period runs and the payday, then tap Save.

notes: Live sync or a file?: Invoices are a live sync: they are posted straight into your package. Payroll is a file: the connection cannot post into payroll, so you get a spreadsheet laid out for BrightPay, QuickBooks, Sage, Moneysoft or Xero, or a general one for anything else. Each choice says whether it matches that product's published import or is set out to match or type in.

One pay run: This is the only payroll file. The Timesheets Payroll file button opens it. It carries hours, overtime, holiday hours and pay (12.07% built up for irregular-hours workers, or rolled-up holiday pay where set), SSP days and pay, and expenses and mileage to repay.

Minimum wage and apprentice rate: Each person’s hourly rate is checked against the minimum for their age, or the apprentice rate, on every day they worked. Anyone below it stops the run until the rate is fixed, or the owner or an admin gives a reason, which is kept with the run.
The holiday record: Each run writes holiday built up, holiday pay and rolled-up pay to the holiday record, kept for 6 years. You see it on each person’s sheet.
Subcontractors: Subcontractors are never in the payroll file. They are paid by self-bill statement with CIS, shown in their own panel with a CIS file.

Nothing goes twice: Every approved entry and claim that goes to payroll is marked with the run that took it. Approve more later and only the new ones go next time. Sent by mistake? Put the run back within 48 hours.

Expenses are paid on payday: Expenses in a run show as In payroll until the run’s payday. Early that morning they are marked Paid with payday as the date, and each worker gets one message with their total. No payday set? The period end date is used, and the review says so. A run with expenses cannot be put back once payday has come.
Who sees what: Owners and admins see pay, expenses and invoices. Office managers see the connection and can send an hours-only file, but never see a rate or a £ figure.

helps.title: Client portal
helps.what: Each client gets one private page with their jobs and dates, who is coming on the day, certificates to download, quotes to accept, invoices with Pay now, and a message thread with you. They open it from a link, with no account or password.
steps: Open the client: Go to Clients and open the client. The Client portal card makes their link the first time you tap Create.
Send it: Copy it, share it, send it by WhatsApp or email, or show the QR code on site. Invoice emails also carry it.
Answer messages: Messages from clients land here, on the client record and in your notifications. Reply from the client record.

tasks.title: Give a client their portal
steps: Tap Share with a client. It opens Clients.
Tap the client, then Create portal link in the Client portal card.
Tap Copy, Share, WhatsApp or Email, or QR code to show it on site.

tasks.title: Reply to a client message
steps: Under Messages, tap the client. Unread ones show a yellow pill.
Their record opens with the thread in view.
Type in the box and tap Send.

tasks.title: Check a client has opened it
steps: Look under Portal links.
Each client shows how many times they opened it and when, or Not shared or opened yet.
Live, Paused or Expired shows on the right.

tasks.title: Pause, expire or switch off a link
steps: Tap the client under Portal links. Their record opens.
In the Client portal card, pick how long the link lasts: No expiry, 30 days, 90 days or 1 year.
Tap Pause to hide it for now, New link if it went to the wrong person, or Switch off to end it for good.

notes: What the client sees: Only their own jobs, certificates, quotes and invoices. Staff appear by first name only, and only if they have switched on "Show me to customers". No phone numbers, costs or safety records.
Certificates: Shown once issued. If you hold a certificate until the invoice is paid, or a QS still has to sign it off, the client sees "Being finalised" until it is released.
Turning a link off: Pause it, give it an expiry, make a new link if it went to the wrong person, or switch it off for good. Messages are kept either way.

helps.title: Team comms
helps.what: Send announcements, job messages and safety alerts to your team, with a record of who read and acknowledged them. Each message is a thread the team can reply in.
steps: Send: New message → everyone, a job’s crew, or chosen people. Tick “Must acknowledge” when you need each person to confirm they have read it. Add photos or PDFs.
Watch it land: The list shows “6 of 8 acknowledged”. Open the message to see exactly who has read it, and chase the rest with one tap.
Talk it through: Replies from the team appear in the thread. Reply to everyone, or tap someone’s reply to answer just them.

tasks.title: Send a message or notice
steps: Tap New message.
Who is it for? Pick Everyone, A job’s crew, or Choose people.
Pick Announcement, Job message or Safety alert. A safety alert asks for acknowledgement unless you untick it.
Tick Must acknowledge if each person has to confirm. Add a title, the message, and any photos or PDFs.
Tap Send to … people.

tasks.title: See who has read it
steps: Tap the message in the list. Each row shows, for example, 6 of 8 acknowledged.
Tap the bar at the top of the thread (it says Who) to see each person.

tasks.title: Chase the people who have not read it
steps: Open the message.
Tap Chase (it shows how many people are left).
Each of them gets a push and a bell. You can chase once an hour.

tasks.title: Answer a reply
steps: Tap New replies to see threads with something new.
Open the thread. Reply to everyone, or tap someone’s reply to answer just them.

notes: Who sees what: A worker sees the message, your replies to everyone, and their own private conversation with the office. They never see each other’s replies. Someone who leaves the team loses access straight away.
Chasing: Chase sends a push and a bell to each person who has not acknowledged (or read) it. Once an hour at most, so nobody gets spammed.
Team chat: For everyday chat use Team chat (channels and direct messages). Use a Comms message when you need the record.

helps.title: Customer inbox
helps.what: Every message with your customers in one place: texts, WhatsApp, email replies and messages from their portal page.
steps: Read and reply: Open a conversation and reply on Text, WhatsApp, Email or Portal. Templates fill in their name, the job and the date for you.
Replies ring the bell: When a customer writes back, the office bell rings and the conversation moves to the top here.
Opt-outs are kept: If a customer replies STOP, nothing more goes to them on that channel until they reply START. You can also mark it yourself.
Test mode: Until texting is switched on for your firm, messages are saved but not sent, so you can try everything safely.

helps.title: Enquiries
helps.what: Every way a customer gets in touch, in one list: your enquiry email address, website form, quote page, missed calls and texts, Checkatrade and MyBuilder forwards, and online bookings. The same enquiries you see in the Electrical Hub.
steps: Read it at a glance: Each enquiry is read for you: the job, how urgent it is, the address and any photos. The original message is kept underneath.
Reply first: Call, text or email from the enquiry. A reply is written for you to check. The first firm to answer usually wins the job.
One tap to a quote or a job: Make a quote or a job and the name, contact, address, job, details and photos go with it. Nothing to retype.
Won when they accept: An enquiry shows as Won only when the customer accepts the quote, so the win rate is real.
notes: The whole customer: Open an enquiry to see everything else with that person: other enquiries, bookings, quotes, jobs and messages.
Who sees it: The owner, admins and office managers. Quote values show only to the owner and admins.

helps.title: Expenses
helps.what: Receipts and mileage your team claims back. You approve them, then pay them in a pay run.
steps: The team claims: Workers photograph a receipt or log mileage on their phone. It lands here waiting for you.
Approve or reject: Open a claim to see the receipt and the job it is for. Reject with a reason so they know what to fix.
Pay them back: Send them with payroll from Accounting and they are marked paid on payday by themselves. Or pay them yourself: Export the list, pay them, then mark them all paid in one go.

tasks.title: Approve a claim
steps: Tap the To approve tab.
Tap the claim. Check the amount, the linked job and tap View receipt if there is one.
Tap Approve. It moves to To pay and counts as a cost on the job.

tasks.title: Send a claim back
steps: Open the claim from To approve.
Tap Reject.
Type the reason, for example the receipt is missing, then tap Reject expense.

tasks.title: Pay everyone in one run
steps: When claims are approved, the Pay back panel shows the total waiting. Tap Pay.
Everyone approved is ticked. Untick a person or a claim to leave it for next time.
Set Paid on to the day the money left, for example payroll day.
Tap Export for a CSV your payroll or bank can use, then tap Mark … paid.

tasks.title: Pay one claim
steps: Tap the To pay tab and open the claim.
Tap Mark as paid. It is marked paid today.

tasks.title: Set the mileage rate
steps: Tap the rate in the Mileage rate panel, then Change.
Pick HMRC approved rate (45p a mile, 25p after 10,000 miles) or Our own rate and type the pence per mile.
Tap Save. New mileage claims use it.
tasks.who: Owner and admins. Everyone else sees the rate but cannot change it.

tasks.title: Add a claim for someone
steps: Tap Add expense.
Basic info: pick the Employee, then the Amount and Description. Tap Continue.
Add the category and job, then a receipt photo or PDF. Tap Continue each time.
Check it on Review & submit and tap Submit expense. It lands in To approve.

notes: In payroll: A claim sent with a payroll run shows In payroll and the payday. On payday it is marked Paid with that date, and the worker gets one message with their total. You do not need to mark it paid.
Mileage rate: Mileage pays at the rate shown in the Mileage rate panel. Change it there if your firm pays a different rate.

helps.title: Right to work and HR records
helps.what: Right-to-work checks for everyone who works for you, how long to keep each record, and, if you use probation, its review dates and when unfair dismissal protection starts.
steps: Check everyone before they start: Open a person and tap Record a check. Pick how you checked, add a copy, and set the follow-up date if their permission is time-limited. People can send their documents or share code from Worker Tools.

Choose warn or block: When someone has no check, assigning them to a job or booking them either warns or stops. Approving hours they have already worked and issuing their statement always go ahead with a warning, because work done must be paid.

Set probation dates, if you use probation: Probation is your choice, not a legal requirement. If you use it, add the end date on the person sheet and you get a reminder 30 days and 7 days before the review, and before the date to decide by.
Clear old records: Records to review lists leavers and applicants whose records have reached the end of their period. Removing them keeps what the law still needs.
notes: Who sees what: Office managers see who is checked. Only the owner and admins see the check details, the copies, probation and the retention queue.

helps.title: Leave
helps.what: Holiday and time-off requests from your team, who is off this week, and how much allowance each person has left.
steps: Set each allowance: Tap a person under Allowances and give them their days for the year. Until you do, they are told to ask the office.
Decide requests: Requests from the app wait at the top. You see who else is off on those days before you approve or decline.
Book leave for someone: Use Book leave for time off agreed in person, so the diary and timesheets know they are away.

tasks.title: Approve a request, checking for clashes
steps: Under Waiting for you, tap the request.
Read Check before you approve: who else is off those days, and any job they are booked on with nobody else on it.
For holiday, check Left after this against their allowance.
Tap Approve. If there is a clash the button says Approve anyway.

tasks.title: Decline a request
steps: Tap the request.
Tap Decline. A box opens.
Say why (at least 3 letters), then tap Send decline.

tasks.title: Book leave for someone
steps: Tap Book leave.
Pick who, the type (Holiday, Sick, Unpaid and so on), Full days, Morning or Afternoon, and the dates.
Already agreed? Pick Yes, book it, or No, add as a request.
Tap Book it (or Add request).

tasks.title: Set someone’s holiday allowance
steps: Under Allowances, tap the person. Not set shows as Set it.
Pick the days they work a week. The legal minimum fills in.
Change Allowance (days) if you give more, and add any Carried over.
Tap Save. They can now see their balance.

notes: The legal minimum: 5.6 weeks a year: 28 days for someone full-time, less pro rata for part-time.

helps.title: Your morning briefing
helps.what: Everything in the firm that needs you today, on one screen. Open it first thing and work down the To do list.
steps: Work the To do list: Most urgent first: safety, then jobs with nobody booked, then approvals and expiring tickets. Each row has one button that takes you straight to it.
Check who's where: Today shows who is on which job, who has clocked in and who is on leave. Tap a person to open their job.
Look at the week: Jobs starting in the next seven days, anything with nobody booked, and leave coming up.

Jump to any part of the hub: Your hub has a card for People, Jobs, Finance, Safety, Clients and Smart Docs. Tap the card for that area, or one of the screens listed under it. A number shows where something is waiting for you.
notes: Who sees the money: The owner and admins see Money. Office managers see everything else on this page, without the figures.
Live numbers: The page updates as your team clocks in, books leave or sends timesheets, and again whenever you come back to it.

helps.title: Policies
helps.what: Your company policies, and proof your team has read them. Each person signs every version in the app, and you can print the policy with its list of signatures.
steps: Start a policy: Adopt one of the templates, or tap Draft with AI and say what it is about. Read it through and fill in anything in square brackets.
Publish it to the team: Everyone on your team who is on the app gets a notification to read and sign it in Worker Tools.
See who has signed: Each policy shows how many have signed, and who is still to. Change a policy and send the new version; everyone signs again.
Show it when asked: Export with signatures gives you the policy and the acknowledgement record in one PDF, for SSIP and principal contractor questionnaires.

helps.title: The price book
helps.what: One price list for the whole firm. It is the same list the owner keeps in the Electrical Hub, so a price changed here is changed there too. Quotes, purchase orders and van stock all use it.
steps: Add what you buy and sell: Add items one by one, import a merchant price list, or save lines from a quote in the Electrical Hub.
Set buy, markup and sell: Give a buy price and markup and the sell price works itself out. Quotes use the sell price.
Keep it honest: When a supplier invoice is matched to an order, the price you actually paid shows against the item, so you spot price rises.

tasks.title: Add an item
steps: On the Items tab, tap Add item.
Give it a name, the unit it is sold by, a category and the usual supplier.
Enter the Buy price (£) and Markup (%), and the sell price works itself out. Or type the Sell price (£) straight in.
Tap Add to price book.

tasks.title: Import a merchant price list
steps: Tap Import.
Choose a CSV or Excel file. Columns are matched by their headings: name or description, price, unit, category and supplier.
Check the rows it found, then tap Import … items.

tasks.title: Bring in your wholesaler account prices
steps: Tap the Wholesalers tab, then Add account. Pick the wholesaler and add your account number, branch and order email.
Ask the branch for your account price file (CSV or Excel). Elec-Mate has no live price link with any wholesaler yet.
Tap Import prices on the account and choose the file. Check the columns, then tick any close matches.
Tap Save. Linked items get the new buy price, and big moves are flagged on open quotes.

tasks.title: Fix the items that need a check
steps: Tap Needs a check. It lists items with no sell price, prices over 60 days old, or a last paid price above the book.
Tap an item and update the price.
Tap Save changes.

tasks.title: Use it in a quote
steps: Go to Quotes & Invoices and tap New quote.
Tap Pick from … price-book items and choose the lines.
They come in at the sell price. Purchase orders use the buy price.

tasks.title: Set your labour rates and markup
steps: Tap the Labour & markup tab.
Enter your Day rate (£), Hourly rate (£) and default Markup (%).
Tap Save rates.
tasks.who: Only the owner can change the rates. Others see them.

notes: Who sees what: Office managers see sell prices only. Buy prices, markup and what you paid are for the owner and admins.
Labour rates: Your day and hourly rates sit under Labour & markup. They feed quotes and job profit.

helps.title: Purchase orders
helps.what: Order materials for a job, track the delivery, and check the supplier bills you what you agreed.
steps: Order from the job: Open a job and tap Materials. The quote fills the order at your price-book buy prices.
Send, then book it in: Nothing goes to the supplier until you tap Send. When it arrives, book in what came.
Match the invoice: Upload the supplier invoice PDF or a photo. Overcharges and short deliveries are flagged, and the cost lands on the job.

tasks.title: Raise a purchase order
steps: On the Orders tab, tap Raise an order. From a job it says Order materials.
Pick the Supplier and the Job. The cost lands on that job once it is sent.
Add lines: Fill from a quote, tap Price book, or type a line. Buy prices come from your price book.
Tap Save draft to keep it, or Save & send to email it now. Save & send only shows when the supplier has an order email.

tasks.title: Send a draft to the supplier
steps: Tap the draft order.
Tap PO as PDF if you want to check it first.
Tap Send to … The PO goes as a PDF to the supplier’s order email.

tasks.title: Book a delivery in
steps: Tap an order that is Sent, Confirmed or Part-received.
Tap Book a delivery in.
Under What arrived, set how many of each came. Add a photo of the delivery note if you have one.
Tap Book in … items. The order moves to Part-received or Received.
tasks.who: Owner, admins and office managers. Quantities only, no prices.

tasks.title: Check the supplier’s invoice
steps: Open a sent order.
Under Supplier invoice, tap Match the invoice (PDF or photo) and pick the file.
It reads the invoice and flags overcharges and short deliveries. Invoices needs a check shows on the order until you have looked.

tasks.title: Add your suppliers
steps: Tap the Suppliers tab.
Tap Add supplier. With none yet, Add the big UK merchants adds Edmundson, CEF, Rexel, YESSS, Screwfix and Denmans.
Open each one and add your account number and their order email.

notes: Who sees prices: Office managers see orders and book deliveries in. Buy prices and invoices are for the owner and admins.
Tools and test kit: PAT and calibration now live in the Kit register.

helps.title: Your quote page
helps.what: A page with your name, colour and logo where a customer asks you for a quote in under a minute, with photos. Every request lands in Leads and Enquiries, and you get a bell, a push and an email.
steps: Fill it in: Add what you do, the areas you cover and the year you started. Your registration scheme and insurance come from Settings, and only show while they are in date.
Put it everywhere: Van QR, Google Business Profile, email signature, Facebook. The link also goes on every invoice and quote email unless you switch that off.
Answer fast: Requests arrive with the job, postcode, timing and photos. The first firm to call usually wins the job.

tasks.title: Set up your page
steps: Under Your page, type a link name. Pick it carefully: changing it later breaks printed QR codes.
Add a headline and a few lines about you, the trading since year, and what you do and areas you cover (type one, then tap +).
Tap Save changes.

tasks.title: Put the page live
steps: At the top, switch on the toggle. It reads Your page is live.
Tap Preview to see what customers see.
Tap Copy or Share to send the short link.

tasks.title: Print a van sign or QR code
steps: Under Get it seen, tap Van sign PDF or A4 poster.
Or tap QR (PNG), or QR (SVG) for a sign-writer.
Scan it with your phone camera before you print.

tasks.title: Add the link to invoices and quotes
steps: Under Get it seen, find Every invoice and quote.
Switch it on. A Get a quote link goes at the bottom of every invoice and quote email while the page is live.

tasks.title: Show your scheme and insurance
steps: Under Proof customers see, switch on Registration scheme or Insurance.
If a switch is greyed out, add the scheme or insurer and expiry in Settings, Company, first.
Anything out of date hides itself.

notes: What customers never see: Your address, email, prices and anything else private. Reviews only show when real customers have left them.
Spam: Requests are rate limited on our side and bots are filtered out before they reach you.

helps.title: Site Safety
helps.what: The Site Safety tools from the Electrical Hub, working on your firm’s records. A RAMS, permit or check made here belongs to the firm, and your managers can open and edit it.
steps: Create a RAMS for a job: Tap Create RAMS, describe the work and generate. It is filed with the firm, not with you.
See your team’s records: When someone on your team files a RAMS, permit or check against one of your jobs, it shows in that tool. You can read it and countersign it; they keep the right to change it.
Look things up: Hazards, emergency procedures, product recalls and HSE guidance are here for everyone.
notes: What stays private: A worker’s own records stay in their Electrical Hub. They reach the firm only when they file one against a firm job.
Kit and photos: The firm’s kit lives in the Kit register and job photos in Job photos, so there is one list of each.

The safety score: Built only from your records: toolbox talks signed, near misses closed, team records countersigned, COSHH in date and RAMS issued. With too little to go on it says Not started, never a perfect score.

helps.title: Timesheets
helps.what: Every hour your team logs lands here. You approve it or send it back, then take the approved hours to the pay run in Accounting.
steps: The team logs time: Workers clock in and out on their phone, or add a past day. You can add an entry for someone too.
Approve or send back: Check the day, the job and the break. Send it back with a reason and the worker can fix it and resubmit.
Send it to payroll: Pay run opens the one payroll file in Accounting: approved hours, overtime, holiday, sick pay and expenses for the pay period, with the minimum wage checked.

tasks.title: Approve the clean entries in one go
steps: Open the Week or Pending tab.
In the Payroll check card, tap Approve all … clean.
Anything flagged (a long day, no job, no break on a long shift, a weekend, no pay rate) stays waiting for you to check one by one.

tasks.title: Check and approve one entry
steps: Open the Pending tab.
Tap the entry. The sheet shows the day, start and finish, break and job.
Tap Approve.

tasks.title: Send a day back to be fixed
steps: Tap the entry to open it.
Tap Reject. A box opens for the reason.
Type what needs fixing (at least 3 letters), then tap Send back.

tasks.title: Approve or send back several at once
steps: Tap Select.
Tap each waiting entry, or Select all waiting.
Tap Approve, or Reject then type one reason and tap Send back. Everyone selected sees that reason.
Tap Done to leave select mode.

tasks.title: Send the hours to payroll
steps: Approve the period first. Only approved hours go.
Tap Pay run. It opens Send to payroll in Accounting.
Pick the pay period and your payroll software, then tap Check and send.
tasks.who: Owner and admins get the file with pay. Office managers get hours only.

tasks.title: Add hours for someone
steps: Tap Add entry.
Pick the worker, the day and the job, then the times and break.
Save it. It lands as waiting, ready to approve.

notes: Timesheet rules: The owner sets the default break and working day under the rules button. They pre-fill clock-outs and manual entries.
Who sees pay: Office managers see hours only and send an hours-only file. Pay rates and the payroll file with pay are for the owner and admins.

helps.title: My pay (subcontractor)
helps.what: Your approved days for each firm you work for and the self-bill statements they send you, with the CIS they deducted.
steps: Submit your days: Clock in and out, or add your days in Timesheets, like the rest of the team.
The firm approves them: Only approved days go on a statement. Waiting days show here.
Get your statement: Each tax month (6th to 5th) the firm sends a statement: labour, materials, CIS deducted and net paid. Keep it for your tax return.
notes: CIS: CIS is taken off labour and other costs only, never materials. What was deducted counts towards your tax bill on your Self Assessment.

helps.title: Pre-start checks
helps.what: The checks your firm wants done on this job. The “before you start” ones are yours to do, and the clock opens once every required one is done.
steps: Do the before-start checks: Tap each one. Ticks save straight away; photos, numbers, yes/no and signatures open a short sheet.
Sign the RAMS: If the firm sent RAMS for this job, the RAMS check sends you to Sign-offs. It turns green when you have signed.
Clock in, then finish off: Once everything required is done, Clock in opens. The on-completion checks appear here, ending with the customer’s signature.
notes: What gets recorded: Your name, the time and where your phone was (once, when you save). If location is off it says so; you can still save.
Yes or no questions: A required yes/no only counts as done when the answer is Yes. Answer No and say why, and the office sees it.
Apprentices: Some checks need your supervisor to countersign. They do it on their phone from this job, or the office does.

helps.title: Expenses
helps.what: Claim back mileage and money you spent on the job. The office approves it and pays you back, with your wages or when they pay expenses.
steps: Log mileage or a receipt: Tap Log mileage or Claim a receipt. Pick the job if it was for one.
Send it to the office: It shows as Waiting. You can change it or withdraw it until the office approves it.
Get paid back: You get a notification when the office decides. Approved money shows under Coming back to you.

tasks.title: Claim mileage
steps: Tap Log mileage.
Type where you set off From and where you went To. Picking a job with an address fills in To for you.
Pick One way or There and back.
Tap Work out miles, or type the miles yourself.
Check the amount under You’ll claim, then tap Send.

tasks.title: Claim a receipt
steps: Tap Claim a receipt.
Tap Take a photo or choose a file, and pick the job if it was for one.
Tap Save it. The receipt is read for you and shows under Receipts and bills.
Tap it there, check the figures and the kind of spend, then tap Post.

tasks.title: Fix a claim that was rejected
steps: Tap the Rejected filter.
Tap the claim. Where it is shows the office’s reason.
A rejected claim cannot be changed. Make a new claim with the fix, using Log mileage or Claim a receipt.

tasks.title: Change or withdraw a waiting claim
steps: Tap the Waiting filter, then tap the claim.
Tap Change it to edit it, or Withdraw then Withdraw claim to remove it.

notes: Where your money is: Waiting is with the office. Coming back to you is approved. Paid back is done. Miles since 6 April show under Mileage rate.

helps.title: Credentials
helps.what: Your qualifications, cards and training, kept on your Elec-ID with a photo of each. You control the list. Your employer’s competence matrix reads the same list, so you only keep it up to date once, and it moves with you if you change firms.
steps: Add what you hold: Tap Add, pick the ticket (ECS, 18th Edition, 2391, First Aid…) or type your own, then add the number, the dates and a photo.
See what your firm needs: If your firm has set what it needs on site, you see each one as Held, Expiring or Missing, with Add it to fill the gap.
Get reminded: We remind you 60 days and 14 days before anything expires, and on the day. Your firm is told 30 days before.
Your employer checks it: What you add shows to your firm as Added by them until someone records that they have seen it or checked it at source.

tasks.title: Add a qualification or card with a photo
steps: Tap Add (on a phone, Add a qualification or card).
Tap one of the usual tickets, or type the Name yourself.
Add the certificate or card number, Achieved and Expires dates if you have them.
Tap Take a photo (or Choose a file for a PDF).
Tap Save. It is added to your Elec-ID as self-declared.

tasks.title: Fill a gap your firm has flagged
steps: Find What your firm needs on this page.
Tap Add it next to anything Missing, or Update next to anything expiring.
Fill in the details and photo, then tap Save.

tasks.title: Update a ticket that is expiring
steps: Tap the Needs attention filter.
Tap the item.
Change the Expires date (and the number if it changed), add a photo of the new one, then tap Save.

tasks.title: Check your reminders
steps: Make sure each item has the right Expires date.
We remind you at 60 days, 14 days and on the day. Your firm hears 30 days before.

tasks.title: Remove something
steps: Tap the item.
Tap Remove from my Elec-ID, then tap again to confirm.

tasks.title: Change your ECS card
steps: Tap Open Elec-ID.
Update the card in your Elec-ID settings.

helps.title: My equipment
helps.what: The company kit on your name or on the van you drive, when each item is due its PAT test or calibration, and the stock on your van.
steps: Confirm what you are given: When the office issues you something, tap I have it so they know it reached you.
Tell the office: Report a fault or a loss with a photo, pass it to someone, or hand it back. The office is told straight away.
Log what you use: In Van stock, log the materials you used on a job. The van stock goes down and the office reorders when it runs low.

tasks.title: Confirm you have something
steps: Open the notification, or find it under Confirm you have this.
Check you have it, then tap I have it.

tasks.title: Report a fault or a loss
steps: Tap the item.
Tap Report a fault (or Report it lost).
Say what is wrong and take a photo.
Tap Send fault report.

tasks.title: Pass kit to someone or hand it back
steps: Tap the item.
Tap Pass to someone and pick who, or Hand it back.
Add a note if it helps and send.

tasks.title: Check what needs a PAT test or calibration
steps: Tap the Due soon filter.
Tap an item to see its dates.

tasks.title: Find kit by scanning it
steps: Tap Scan.
Point the camera at the barcode or serial label.

tasks.title: Log materials used on a job
steps: Tap Van stock.
Tap Log materials used on a job.
Pick the job.
Tap + on each thing you used, or tap Scan and scan the box.
Tap Log.

tasks.title: Count the van
steps: Tap Van stock.
Tap the item.
Enter how many are really on the van and tap Save count.

notes: Something missing or wrong?: The office issues kit and sets up van stock in the Kit register. Ask them to add or change it.
Prices: You see names and quantities only. The office handles the costs.

helps.title: Progress notes
helps.what: An end of day update on a job: what is done, what is next, anything in the way. It goes to the office and whoever is on the job next sees it.
steps: Pick the job: Only shows if you are on more than one job.
Say or type it: Type the note, or tap Speak and talk. Add photos if they help.
Send to the office: It is stamped with your name and time. You can change or delete it for 24 hours.

tasks.title: Log today’s progress
steps: Pick the job, if you are on more than one.
Type what is done, what is next and anything in the way, or tap Speak.
Tap Add photos if you want to show it.
Tap Send to the office.

tasks.title: Change or delete a note
steps: Find your note under On this job.
Tap Change to edit the words or photos, then save.
Or tap Delete, then Tap again to delete.

tasks.title: Use a note as OTJ evidence (apprentices)
steps: Find your note under On this job.
Tap Use as OTJ evidence.
Finish the entry and send it for sign-off.

helps.title: Reports
helps.what: Raise a snag, a near-miss or an incident on a job. Snags go to the snag log. Near-misses and incidents go straight to the office’s incident log.
steps: Pick what it is: Snag for a quality defect. Near-miss for a close call. Incident for a safety event.
Fill it in: Pick the job and severity, say what happened, where, and add photos if it is safe to.
Submit it: The office sees it straight away. Its history shows on the right.

tasks.title: Raise a snag
steps: Tap Snag.
Choose the job.
Pick Minor, Moderate or Critical.
Describe the issue and where it is on site.
Tap Add photos if it helps, then tap Submit snag.

tasks.title: Report a near-miss or an incident
steps: Tap Near-miss or Incident.
Choose the job and the severity.
Say what happened, factually: what you saw and what was affected.
Add a photo of the hazard if it is safe to, then tap Submit.

tasks.title: Close a safety action the office gave you
steps: Safety actions for you shows at the top when the office has given you one.
Do the action, then tap Done next to it.

helps.title: QS reviews
helps.what: Certificates sent to a Qualifying Supervisor (QS) for sign-off. You see why any of yours came back. If you have the QS role, you also countersign or return your team’s, right here, without the Employer Hub.
steps: Open a certificate: Tap one. Returned ones show first and need you to act.
See why it came back: The reasons your QS ticked and their comments sit at the top, then notes against each circuit or observation.
Fix and resubmit: Tap Edit certificate, make the changes, then Resubmit to QS.

tasks.title: Act on your QS’s feedback
steps: Tap Returned.
Tap the certificate. Why it came back is at the top.
Read the comments. Reply with Add comment if you need to.
Tap Edit certificate and make the changes.
Come back and tap Resubmit to QS.

tasks.title: Countersign a certificate (QS only)
steps: Tap To review, then Waiting. The oldest is first.
Tap the certificate and check the detail. Use View PDF to see it as printed.
Tap Approve & countersign.
Check your name, sign, add a comment if you want, then tap Confirm approval.
tasks.who: Only people with the QS role see To review.

tasks.title: Send a certificate back with reasons (QS only)
steps: Open the certificate from Waiting.
Tap + Comment against a circuit or observation to point at the exact problem.
Tap Return with reasons, tick what is wrong and add a note if it helps.
Tap Return certificate. The electrician is told why straight away.
tasks.who: Only people with the QS role.

notes: Common returns: On To review, Common returns counts the reasons ticked over the last 20 decisions, so the team can see what keeps coming back.

helps.title: Confirm apprentice hours
helps.what: Off-the-job training logged by apprentices you supervise. Confirm what you saw happen, or send it back with what needs changing. Their college checks it separately.
steps: You get a notification: When an apprentice you supervise logs hours, they show here.
Read the entry: The day, the hours, the type of training and what they did.
Confirm or send back: Confirm marks the hours as workplace-confirmed. Send back asks them to change it.

tasks.title: Confirm an entry
steps: Read the entry.
Tap Confirm.

tasks.title: Send an entry back
steps: Tap Send back.
Say what they need to change (at least 5 letters).
Tap Send back again.

notes: Who can confirm: The apprentice’s named workplace supervisor, and the team’s supervisors, project managers and apprentice co-ordinators. You only see entries you can act on.

helps.title: Your crew
helps.what: Timesheets, expenses and leave from the people who name you as their supervisor. Approve them or send them back. The office sees everything you decide.
steps: Requests come in: Grouped as Timesheets, Expenses and Leave.
Check each one: Who it is from, the day or amount, and any note.
Approve or send back: Send back needs a reason, which the person sees.

tasks.title: Approve a request
steps: Check the details.
Tap Approve.

tasks.title: Send a request back
steps: Tap Send back.
Say what they need to change.
Tap Send back again.

notes: Who is in your crew: The office sets who you supervise on each person in Team. Until then, approvals stay with the office.

helps.title: My van
helps.what: The van the office has put on your name. Do the walk-round check before you drive it each day, and report anything wrong with a photo so the office can get it fixed.
steps: Check it every day: Tap Start today’s check. Enter the mileage, then tap OK or Problem for each item. It takes about a minute.
Photo anything wrong: Tap Problem, then Take a photo. Add a short note if it helps. The office sees the photo straight away.
Say if it is safe: If it is not safe to drive, choose No, take it off the road. The office is told and the van is marked off the road.
Report a problem any time: Something goes wrong mid-day? Tap Report a problem. You do not need to do the whole check again.

tasks.title: Do today’s check
steps: Tap Start today’s check.
Type the mileage on the dash and tap Next.
For each item tap OK or Problem. Rest all OK fills in anything you have not answered.
For a problem, take a photo and add a note.
On the last screen say whether it is safe to drive, then tap Send check.

tasks.title: Report a problem
steps: Tap Report a problem.
Pick what is wrong, or Something else.
Tap Take a photo. Add a note.
Say whether it is safe to drive, then tap Send to the office.
