notes: Off the road: A van marked off the road should not be driven until the office puts it back on. The card on this page shows when it is.
No van showing?: The office assigns vans in Fleet. If you drive one and it is not here, ask them to put it on your name.
Who sees your check: Your employer’s office. Photos are private to your firm.

helps.title: Worker Tools
helps.what: Everything from your firm in one place: your hours, jobs, sign-offs, leave, pay and messages from the office.
steps: Start with To do now: Anything the office needs from you shows here first: a day sent back, a new job, a pack to sign, tasks due.
Clock in from the top: Clock in, Request leave and your status are the three buttons at the top. Clock in takes you to Timesheets.
Find any tool below: Tools lists every page: timesheets, jobs, my week, tasks, sign-offs, expenses, leave, pay and more.

tasks.title: Deal with what the office needs
steps: Look at To do now.
Tap an item. It opens the right page, for example the day that was sent back.

tasks.title: Clock in for the day
steps: Tap Clock in at the top.
On Timesheets, tap Clock in, pick the job and tap Start the clock.

tasks.title: Find a tool
steps: Scroll to Tools.
Tap the one you need. A number on a tool means something is waiting there.

helps.title: My status
helps.what: Tell the office where you are: On Site, En Route, Office or Off Duty. They see it on their live board.
steps: Pick a status: Tap On Site, En Route, Office or Off Duty.
Pick the job: On Site and En Route need the job you are on or heading to.
Tap Set to …: On Site and En Route share your location once, when you save. Office and Off Duty never ask for it.

tasks.title: Say you’re on site or on the way
steps: Tap On Site or En Route.
Under Which job?, choose the job.
Tap Set to On Site (or Set to En Route).

tasks.title: Finish for the day
steps: Tap Off Duty.
Tap Set to Off Duty. No location is asked for.

notes: Who else sets it: The office can set your status, and clocking in or out sets it. You get a message on screen when that happens.

helps.title: My pay
helps.what: What your approved hours and expenses add up to, and when payday is. It is an estimate before tax, not a payslip.
steps: Pick the pay period: This pay period or Last pay period. If your firm has no payday set, you see this week or this month instead.
Read the figure: Approved hours at the rate the office has for you, with overtime. Hours waiting for approval are not counted yet.
Check it went to payroll: Sent to payroll shows when the office sent your hours. Expenses to be repaid shows approved claims.

tasks.title: See what you’ve earned this period
steps: Tap This pay period (or Last pay period).
Read the big figure and the payday under it.
Approved, Awaiting approval and Expenses to be repaid sit underneath.

tasks.title: Check your hours went to payroll
steps: Look at Sent to payroll.
It lists each batch of your hours the office sent, and the date.
Approved days not sent yet go in the next one.

notes: Your rate: The rate badge at the top is what the office has on your record. If it says Rate not set, you see hours only. Ask the office.

helps.title: Leave
helps.what: Book time off, see how much holiday you have left, and follow each request.
steps: Tap Request: Pick the type: annual, sick, unpaid, compassionate or training.
Pick the dates: Or a half day. You see how many days it uses and if anyone else is off.
Submit it: The office approves or declines. If they decline, their reason shows on the request.

tasks.title: Book time off
steps: Tap Request (Request Leave on a computer).
Pick the leave type.
Set the start and end dates, or turn on Half Day and pick morning or afternoon.
Check the days it uses and whether others are off. Add a reason if you like.
Tap Submit Request.

tasks.title: Withdraw a request or cancel leave
steps: Find it under Your Requests.
Tap Withdraw request (still pending) or Cancel leave (approved, not started yet).
Tap Yes to confirm, or Keep it.

tasks.title: See why a request was declined
steps: Tap the Declined tab.
The office’s reason shows under the request.

helps.title: Team comms
helps.what: Messages from the office. Read them, reply with a question, and acknowledge the ones that ask you to.
steps: Open a message: Unread ones are marked. To acknowledge shows the ones the office needs you to confirm.
Acknowledge if asked: Messages marked Please acknowledge have an Acknowledge button. The office sees when you did.
Reply if unsure: Type in Reply to the office. Your reply goes to the office only.

tasks.title: Read and acknowledge a message
steps: Tap To acknowledge.
Tap the message to open it.
Read it, then tap Acknowledge.

tasks.title: Reply to the office
steps: Open the message.
Type in Reply to the office at the bottom. You can attach a photo or PDF.
Send it.

tasks.title: Chat with the team
steps: Tap Team chat.
Pick a channel or a direct message.

helps.title: My jobs
helps.what: Every job the office has put you on, with the site contact, access notes, drawings, packs to sign and who else is on it.
steps: Open a job: New from the office is at the top. Tap a job for directions, the contact and the office’s notes.
Work the job: Clock in, see your tasks, add a progress note or report an issue from On this job.
Finish your part: Tap I’ve finished my part. The office gets told, and when everyone is done the job moves to Testing.

tasks.title: Open a job and get there
steps: Tap the job.
Tap Directions for the map.
Read Getting in, From the office and About the job.

tasks.title: Tell the office you’ve finished your part
steps: Open the job.
Tap I’ve finished my part.
Say what’s done and anything left, and add photos if you like.
Tap Tell the office.

tasks.title: Clock in, tasks, notes or a problem on this job
steps: Open the job.
Under On this job tap Clock in, My tasks, Progress note or Report an issue.

tasks.title: See who else is on site today
steps: Open a job that is on today.
Read Crew on site: who is on the job and who has clocked in.
The small map shows the job and anyone clocked in on it.

helps.title: My week
helps.what: Where you are booked each day, straight from the office’s diary, with drive times and who moved what.
steps: Pick the week: Use the arrows. Back to this week brings you home.
Read each day: Job, client, time and the drive from the yard or the last job. Leave shows as a striped day.
Spot changes: Latest changes and the Moved by tag show who changed your bookings and when.

tasks.title: See next week
steps: Tap the right arrow.
Tap Back to this week to come back.

tasks.title: Open a job or get directions
steps: Tap a booking to open the job.
Tap Directions to … for the map.

tasks.title: Check what the office changed
steps: Read Latest changes at the top.
A Moved by or Booked by tag on a job shows a change in the last week.

helps.title: My tasks
helps.what: Jobs within the job: what the office has given you, grouped by job. The office sees each change straight away.
steps: Start one: Tap Start when you pick a task up.
Mark it done: Tap Done when it is finished. Blocked? Open it and tap Blocked.
Add updates: Open a task to add a photo or write an update for the office.

tasks.title: Start and finish a task
steps: On To do, tap Start on the task.
When it’s finished, tap Done.

tasks.title: Say a task is blocked
steps: Tap the task to open it.
Under Update status, tap Blocked.
Write why in the update box and send it.

tasks.title: Add a photo or an update
steps: Open the task.
Tap Add photo, or type in the update box and tap send.

tasks.title: Pick up a spare task
steps: Look at Up for grabs on your jobs.
Tap I’ll take it.

helps.title: Sign-offs
helps.what: Job packs (RAMS, method statements, briefings) the office needs you to read and sign before you start.
steps: Open a pack: Waiting for your signature is at the top.
Read it: Scope of works, required credentials, the briefing and documents.
Sign it: Draw your signature and tap Sign and confirm. The office is notified.

tasks.title: Read and sign a pack
steps: Tap To sign.
Tap the pack.
Read the scope, credentials, briefing and documents.
Draw your signature in Your signature.
Tap Sign and confirm.

tasks.title: Check what you signed
steps: Tap Signed.
Tap a pack. The signature record shows who signed and when.

helps.title: Your college
helps.what: Everything your college asks of you and everything it has recorded about you, in one place. Your tutor sees the same figures.
steps: Start with Do next: Anything waiting on you is at the top, most urgent first. Tap a row and it opens the exact place to deal with it.
Check where you stand: Each card under Your college says in words how that part is going: criteria passed, hours counted, goals open.
Add your view before a review: Every three months you, your tutor and your employer meet. Tell your tutor how you think it is going first.
notes: Off-the-job hours: The hours figure is the same one your tutor sees: hours your tutor or employer has signed off, plus learning time the app measured. Hours waiting on your tutor are not counted yet.
Criteria passed: Only your assessor can mark a criterion passed. Evidence you have claimed or sent counts once they decide.

helps.title: Your college area
helps.what: One part of your college area: lessons, your learning plan, quizzes and hours, assessment, your end-point assessment, surveys or your record. Everything here is about you; your college sees the same.
steps: Do what is waiting: Anything your tutor has set or is waiting on is at the top. Tap it to deal with it.
Keep your evidence moving: Your portfolio, witness statements and assessor decisions live under Progress and assessment.
No college yet?: Your portfolio, hours and study all work without one. Join with your college or cohort code when you have it, or invite an assessor yourself.
notes: Who sees what: Your college tutor and assessor see your portfolio, hours and quiz results. An assessor you invite sees your evidence and can record decisions until you remove them.

helps.title: Road to Gold Card
helps.what: What to do after your AM2S to get your ECS Gold Card, and then your JIB grade. Each step links to the ECS or NET page it comes from.
steps: Follow the steps in order: MyECS, the ECS Health, Safety and Environmental Assessment, your documents, then the application.
Tick each one when done: Your tutor sees how far you have got, so they can help if you get stuck.
Check the official page: ECS and the JIB set the rules and can change them. Read their page before you pay for anything.

helps.title: NET’s AM2S checklist
helps.what: NET will not book your AM2S without its Candidate Checklist, signed by you, your employer and your college. This is NET’s own form, filled in here.
steps: Rate yourself honestly: For every item, tick one box for Knowledge and one for Experience. NET says you are unlikely to pass if you cannot confidently tick at least Adequate for every one.
Talk it through: NET finds a three-way talk with your employer and tutor works best. Your tutor sees the same form and can change it with you.
Sign when it is true: Signing opens when every item is at least Adequate. If you change an answer later, everyone who signed signs again.

helps.title: Assessor workspace
helps.what: Every apprentice who has invited you to assess their portfolio, and for each one their evidence against every criterion of their qualification.
steps: Open a learner: The count on each card is criteria the learner has put forward that have no decision yet.
Decide each criterion: Open a criterion to see the evidence mapped to it. Pass it, or send it back with what more is needed. The learner sees your feedback.
Keep your profile current: Your qualifications show next to your name, and each decision you record keeps a copy of them.
notes: Access: You see only the learners who invited you, for as long as their invite stands. No subscription is needed.

helps.title: An assessment criterion
helps.what: Everything about one assessment criterion: what it says, where each learner on the qualification stands against it, the resources that teach it and the lessons that cover it.
steps: See who is behind: Every learner on a course for this qualification is listed with where they stand: passed, submitted, claimed, needs more or not started. Tap one to open their record.
Plan a lesson for it: Plan a lesson for this criterion opens the same lesson composer as the lesson plans list, with this criterion already picked.
Check coverage: Lessons that map to this criterion are listed. If none do, it is a gap in the scheme of work.
notes: Where the status comes from: For a learner with an account it is the same criterion state they and their assessor see in the portfolio. A learner who has not joined yet shows the older college record, if there is one.

helps.title: Learner notebook
helps.what: Ask a question about one learner and get an answer written from their record: criteria met, quiz attempts, off-the-job hours, observations, end-point judgements and their learning plan. It is AI, so check anything you act on.
steps: Pick a learner: Your assigned learners are listed. If none are assigned to you, you see everyone at the college.
Ask: Type a question or tap a ready one. Answers cite the evidence they used.
Act on it: Suggested actions, like booking an observation, can be filed in one tap.

helps.title: Compare cohorts
helps.what: Up to three cohorts side by side: progress, attendance, off-the-job hours, EPA readiness and who is at risk. The best figure in each row is green and the weakest is orange, so the outlier stands out.
steps: Pick the cohorts: Tap up to three. The first three are picked for you; tap one to take it out and another to add it.
Read across a row: Each row is one measure. Green is the best of the selection, orange the weakest. Off-the-job hours are compared per learner.
Go to the cohort: Open a cohort from the Cohorts page to see its learners and act on what you found.
notes: Criteria passed: Each learner’s share of their qualification’s criteria that an assessor has passed or an IQA has confirmed, averaged across the cohort’s learners who have joined. The same count as their portfolio.
At risk: Lower is better: the cohort with the smallest share of learners at risk is green.

helps.title: Gateway readiness
helps.what: Every apprentice’s road to end-point assessment on one page: how far through their practice and portfolio they are, which gateway items are still open, and the verdict on whether they are ready.
steps: Start with your learners: My learners shows the cohorts you lead. Switch to Whole college for the whole college.
Read the orange items: Each learner lists what the gateway still needs. Tap an orange item to go straight to where it is fixed: their portfolio, hours, or the gateway checklist.
Sign off the verdict: When the assisted prediction is newer than yours, the learner shows Needs your sign-off. Open them and record your verdict.
notes: The verdict: The tutor’s verdict counts. Where there is none, the assisted prediction shows, marked as a prediction, until a tutor signs it off.
Same picture as the learner: Readiness is the model the apprentice sees in their own app, so you are both looking at the same thing.

Sort by forecast, filter Off pace: The sort button steps through to Soonest forecast: the earliest gateway forecast first, with anyone who will not get there at this pace last. Off pace lists everyone behind or close to their planned end.

helps.title: AM2 practice on site
helps.what: How often each apprentice does safe isolation, inspection and testing and fault finding at work, from what they tag in evidence and their site diary.
steps: Learners and tutors tag: Evidence and diary days are tagged with the three areas. The app suggests tags from what was written; nothing counts until someone taps it.
Spot the gaps: Orange means none of that area on site in the college’s number of weeks. Learners with most gaps are at the top.
Tutor and employer are told: Each Monday, the tutor gets a bell and the employer an email with their usual link, at most once per area per that many weeks.
notes: Why these three: NET’s survey of first-time AM2 fails: 44% lacked confidence in fault finding, 36% in inspection and testing, and 25% had no regular inspection and testing on site.
When the clock starts: From the learner’s start date, but not before 10 October 2026, when tagging began. Only learners on an AM2-family course are alerted.

helps.title: Learners and billing
helps.what: How Elec-Mate charges your college, using your own numbers: the learners counted for this academic year, the cohorts your agreement covers, invoices and your renewal date.
steps: Counted once a year: At the start of the academic year Elec-Mate counts every learner on a linked cohort. That is the number for the whole year. Nobody is counted again at a new intake or each term.
No seats: A learner who leaves part way through costs nothing more and there is nothing to archive or free up. They keep their own account and record.
Invoices: Elec-Mate sends invoices to your purchase order, paid by bank transfer. They appear here once sent, and show as paid when the money arrives.
notes: Who sees this page: College admins and heads of department. Elec-Mate records the count and the invoices; if anything looks wrong, use Help and support to tell us.

helps.title: Data and API
helps.what: Get your college data out of Elec-Mate for your MIS: download it, or give your MIS team a read-only key. Every export and API call is logged.
steps: Download a dataset: Pick CSV for a spreadsheet or JSON for a developer. Download everything gives one ZIP with every dataset and a manifest.
Fill the ILR fields: Tap a learner to add their ULN, learner reference and the other ILR fields, so the ILR export is ready for your MIS team.

Report in Power BI: The reporting datasets give one row per learner for criteria progress, hours, reviews, risk and attendance. The Power BI guide on this page connects them with a read-only key and refreshes on a schedule.
Create a key: A college admin creates a key, ticks what it can read and sends it to the MIS team securely. It is shown once.
notes: Two ILR outputs: The ILR CSV uses ILR 2026/27 field names for your MIS team to map. The ILR return builds the 2026/27 XML file itself and checks it against the published schema and the validation rules our data can trigger. Submit learner data still runs every rule when you upload, so we never call the file DfE validated.
Keys are never stored: We keep a fingerprint of each key, never the key itself. A lost key cannot be recovered, only revoked and replaced.

helps.title: Bring evidence across
helps.what: Import learners’ evidence from another e-portfolio’s export, so switching mid-programme loses nothing. Each learner checks their items before they join their record.
steps: Export from the old system: Get a CSV with one row per evidence item (learner, title, criteria, assessor, date, outcome, file names), and the files themselves, loose or in a ZIP.
Match the columns: We guess which column is which from the headers. Check each one; only learner and title are required.
Check and import: You see which rows matched a learner, which criteria were read and which files were found, before anything is saved.
Learners confirm: Each learner sees the items on their Today page and adds or leaves out each one.
notes: Not a connection to the old system: We read a file you export. We do not connect to OneFile, Bud, Smart Assessor, Aptem or any other system.

Decisions carried over: For items the learner adds whose original outcome was a pass, an assessor can record an imported decision. It names who recorded it, and keeps the original assessor, date and outcome in its feedback.

helps.title: The evidence pack
helps.what: Everything the apprenticeship funding rules say a college must hold for each apprentice, checked live against your records. It replaces the folder you keep for an audit: what is in place, what is missing, and who it affects. Nothing to keep up to date by hand.
steps: See the gaps: Start with the biggest gap, or use the matrix: one row per learner, one square per piece of evidence.
File the evidence: Open a learner, tap the item and add the document with who signed it. The square turns green.
Hand it over: Print any learner’s pack for an auditor or inspector, or export the whole grid as a spreadsheet.
Add your own: Under Your requirements, add anything else you want on every pack: an induction, a DBS check, a PPE record.
notes: Documents are kept, never overwritten: Filing again creates a new version; the old one is kept and marked replaced, with a fingerprint showing the file is unaltered. Only your college’s staff can see them.
Your own requirements: Anything you add under Your requirements appears on every matching learner’s pack and is chased the same way: inductions, DBS checks, PPE records.

helps.title: Joining your college
helps.what: Your college sent you this link so your Elec-Mate account is linked to them. Once you join, your tutor can see your progress and you can see your college plan.
steps: Sign in or create an account: Use the email your college has for you if you can; it links you to your place on their roll straight away.
We link you automatically: The code in this link is kept while you sign up, so you never have to type it.
Open your college plan: You land on your college plan: your cohort, your tutor, timetable and what is due.
notes: Discount codes: If your college has a discount with Elec-Mate, this join code carries it: it is applied when you create your account. A separate discount code from your college works too.
Already in another college: If you have moved, move your record here in one step. Every decision, witness statement and hour comes with you, and your old college stops seeing it.

helps.title: MIS sync
helps.what: Keep learner references, ULNs and programme dates in step with your MIS by importing its export file. Map a file once, save it, and re-run it each time.
steps: Bring a file: A CSV export of learners or enrolments from ebs, ProSolution, UNIT-e or another MIS, or the ILR XML file your MIS builds.
Map it once: Say which column is which, how dates are written, and which group code is which cohort. Save it with a name.
Check, then apply: The check shows who each row matches, exactly what would change and who is new. Nothing changes until you apply.
notes: What it changes: Only fields the file has a value for and that differ: ULN, learner reference, date of birth, NI number, start, planned end and actual end. A learner in a different cohort is reported, never moved.
Matching: By learner reference first, then ULN, then email. A row that matches nobody becomes a new learner only if it has a name and an email.

helps.title: NET’s AM2S checklist
helps.what: NET needs its Candidate Checklist, the technical qualification and Level 2 maths and English before an AM2S booking. This is NET’s own form: filled in here, exported on NET’s PDF.
steps: Rate it with the apprentice: NET: completed by the apprentice with input from the employer and training provider. You and the apprentice see and change the same answers.
Get three signatures: The apprentice signs in the app, the employer signs through a link with no account, and you sign the training provider declaration. Signing needs every item at least Adequate.
Download the booking pack: A cover sheet with the gateway checks and what to attach, then NET’s complete, filled checklist. Send it to the assessment centre, not to NET head office.
notes: If an answer changes after signing: Earlier signatures stay on record but are left off NET’s form, and show “Sign again”.
Six months: NET only accepts dated signatures within 6 months of the gateway application. The page shows the date to apply by.

helps.title: Ready to start
helps.what: One checklist per learner of what the funding rules need before an apprenticeship starts, with who confirmed each item and the paragraph it meets.
steps: Start onboarding: Open a learner, start onboarding and send them and their employer their links. Nobody needs a new account.

They confirm and sign: The learner confirms eligibility and residency, uploads their ID and signs the apprenticeship agreement on their phone. The employer confirms the employment, signs the agreement and confirms the contract for services.

You check and finish: Check the ID against the originals, and complete the initial assessment, prior learning and training plan in Student 360. When every item is done the learner shows as ready to start.
notes: Signatures that stand up: Each confirmation stores exactly what was confirmed, by whom and when, with a fingerprint chained to the one before. Nothing can be edited or deleted (funding rules 2026/27, paras 346 and 347).
ID copies: Uploads go to your college’s private evidence store, readable only by your staff. Only the document type is recorded, never its number.
Evidence pack: Every completed item appears in the learner’s evidence pack with its paragraph.

helps.title: Off-the-job hours
helps.what: Every learner’s off-the-job training against the total their standard requires. Time spent learning in Elec-Mate is measured as it happens and counts; you approve it.
steps: Approve app learning: One tap approves a learner, a day or the whole view. It is marked verified with your name.
Leave out what does not count: Open a learner’s days and leave out time that does not meet the rules, with a reason they will see.
Watch the monthly check: The rules expect some training every month. Learners with none this month are flagged.
notes: Diary and work activities: What learners log themselves waits in Hours to verify.

Confirmed by apprentices: Register days and site diary days come to the apprentice as hours to confirm, so nobody types them twice. A register day kept to the lesson length counts straight away with the register marker’s name; anything else waits in Hours to verify. Each row says where it came from.

helps.title: Progress reviews
helps.what: Every apprentice needs a three-way review with you and their employer at least every 3 calendar months. This page shows who is due, who is overdue and who still has to sign.
steps: Book the next one: Tap a learner who is due and schedule it. Their employer is added once and used every time.
Send the employer their link: They add their view in two minutes with no account. The invitation is kept as evidence they were asked.
Hold it and sign off: Everything the record knows is filled in. Work through the six steps, agree actions, and sign off; the apprentice and employer sign after.
notes: What counts as overdue: A review on 1 August means the next is due by 30 November: the end of the third calendar month after.
The employer: They must attend most reviews. When they cannot, the link they were sent is the evidence they were given the chance to contribute.

helps.title: Setting up your college
helps.what: Everything a new college needs before its first learner signs in, in order. Each step ticks itself off when it is done; you can come back to this page at any time.
steps: Courses, then cohorts: Pick the qualifications you deliver from the catalogue, then make a cohort on one of them with its dates and lead tutor.
Your staff: Paste name, email and role for each person. New people get a login by email; anyone who already uses Elec-Mate gets a link to join.

Your safeguarding lead: Open the person in Staff and mark them designated safeguarding lead, with a deputy if you have one. They need a login: concerns raised in the app go straight to them, and until one is named they go to admins and heads of department.
Your learners: Paste your MIS list. Each learner gets a login and their cohort join link by email. Running the same list twice is safe.
The join code: Each cohort has one. Learners can also type it on the sign-up page: it links them to the cohort and applies your college discount.
notes: Who can create a college: Elec-Mate issues a set-up code with a signed order. One account belongs to one college.

helps.title: Security and procurement
helps.what: The documents your IT lead, data protection officer and procurement team ask for before the college signs, written from how the system actually works.
steps: Read or download: Pick a document to read it here. Download saves it as a file that opens in any browser; Print lets you save it as a PDF.
Square brackets: Text in square brackets is for your college or Elec-Mate to complete, such as company details or your DPO’s risk ratings.
Questions: Send anything the pack does not answer to … .

helps.title: Try it on your phone
helps.what: Put this on the screen at the end of a demo. Each person who scans the code gets their own demo learner account at the demo college, on their own phone, signed in already.
steps: Show the code: One code lets one person in. As soon as they are in, the next code appears.
They scan it: The phone camera opens a link. In a few seconds they are a learner in a demo cohort, with a demo tutor, lessons and quizzes.
It tidies itself up: Each visit lasts two hours. The account is shut then, and deleted after 48 hours.
notes: Limits: Ten visitors a day for the demo college and three per network an hour, so a code that gets shared cannot fill the college with accounts.
Safe by design: Visitors only ever join the demo college, in a cohort led by a demo tutor. Nothing they do reaches a real college, tutor or learner, and no email is sent.

helps.title: Apprenticeship units
helps.what: Short Apprenticeship Units (ILR programme type 34) next to your full apprenticeships: their own criteria, planned hours and completion, without progress reviews or gateway.
steps: Set up a unit programme: Name it, pick its criteria set and enter the planned hours and the LARS learning aim reference from the unit specification.
Put learners on it: Add a cohort for the course as usual. Learners on it use the same portfolio and hours log.
Record completion: When every criterion is achieved, record the end date. The ILR export shows CompStatus 2 and programme type 34.
notes: What is switched off: Progress reviews (and their inbox items and counts) and gateway and EPA readiness. Everything else stays: portfolio, assessment, IQA, hours, attendance.
What you supply: The unit criteria from your awarding organisation, the learning aim reference, the planned hours, and how your MIS records the outcome. Elec-Mate does not write unit content.

helps.title: Your month in numbers
helps.what: What your staff and learners did in Elec-Mate this month, counted from your own records and set against last month. Use it in team meetings, with governors and at renewal.
steps: Pick the month: The arrows step back through earlier months. Each figure compares with the month before it.
Read the change: Green means up on last month, orange means down where down is worse (for decision time, down is better).
Download it: Download PDF gives a clean copy of the month for a meeting pack.
notes: Nothing is estimated: Every number is a count of real records: hours verified, submissions given a decision, registers taken, messages sent and so on.
At-risk learners: Learners currently flagged high or critical, and how many had contact recorded this month (a note, 1-2-1, concern, flag or intervention).

helps.title: Compliance
helps.what: Everything an inspector, auditor or awarding body could ask to see, in one place: staff records and policies, a live Ofsted readiness view, your self-assessment, the improvement plan and a printable audit pack.
steps: Keep the vault in date: Staff checks (DBS, right to work, references) and policies live in Vault and policies. Expired and missing items show first.
Check your readiness: Ofsted readiness reads your live records against the areas Ofsted inspects and shows where evidence is thin.
Write it up and act on it: Draft the self-assessment, turn its weaknesses into improvement plan actions, and rehearse the questions.
Print the pack: The audit pack puts the single central record, policies, sign-offs and the IQA chain into one document.
notes: Evidence search: Type a question the way an inspector would ask it, such as “show me struggling learners and our response”, and see the learners and records on file that answer it. The question is read with AI; the records are your own.

helps.title: The audit pack
helps.what: One document for an inspector, auditor or awarding body: your single central record, live policies, who has signed each policy, the staff compliance matrix, the IQA verification chain with the sampling rate, the standardisation record and the intervention history.
steps: Check the summary: Expired and missing checks show at the top. Fix them in the vault first if you can.
Read the document: Everything below the summary is the record the PDF is built from.
Download the PDF: Use the button at the top. The PDF is made fresh from the live record, ready to hand to an inspector or auditor.
notes: Always live: The pack is built from your records each time you open it, so it is only as current as the vault.

helps.title: Lesson plan settings
helps.what: What every lesson plan generated for your college must include, and the safeguarding names and wording it can use.
steps: Choose what is always in: British values, stretch and challenge, and inclusive practice. Each is on by default, matching Ofsted and DfE expectations for FE.
Add your names: Your designated safeguarding lead and Prevent lead, so plans name the right people.
Save: The next plan anyone at your college generates uses these settings.
notes: Looking for risk flags?: The attendance target and the gaps that flag a learner at risk are on Quality thresholds, in Settings.

helps.title: Evidence timeline
helps.what: Everything on record for one learner, newest first: learning plan goals, portfolio, quizzes, observations, off-the-job hours, notes, messages, EPA verdicts and IQA. It is the page to open when someone asks you to prove it.
steps: Pick a window: Ninety days shows by default. Widen to twelve months or all time for a full history.
Narrow to one kind: Tap a kind, or a bar in the chart, to see only that evidence.
Open the source: Each row opens where the evidence lives, so you can show the original.
Evidence pack: Evidence pack makes a PDF with every criterion, decision, file and hour, for a handover or an inspector.

helps.title: Practice inspection
helps.what: A safe place to practise the questions an inspector asks. Mate plays the lead inspector, asks one probing question at a time using your college’s real figures, and grades each answer.
steps: Pick a focus: Choose a general inspection or one of Ofsted’s evaluation areas, such as safeguarding or achievement.
Answer as you would on the day: Use real examples and name the evidence. Each answer is graded strong, adequate or insufficient, with feedback.
Finish for a verdict: Each area you were asked about gets the grade your answers would most likely support, with a reason, plus strengths and weaknesses for your improvement plan.
notes: How it grades: Ofsted’s renewed framework grades evaluation areas on five points: exceptional, strong standard, expected standard, needs attention, urgent improvement. Safeguarding is met or not met, and there is no overall grade. The rehearsal grades only the areas it asked about. It is practice, not a prediction.
Who sees it: You can see your own rehearsals. Admins and heads of department at your college can also read them; other tutors cannot.

helps.title: Internal quality assurance
helps.what: Where you check that assessors are making sound, consistent decisions. Plan what to sample, sample it, give a verdict, turn any problems into actions and close them, and keep a record of standardisation.
steps: Set a sampling plan: Pick the qualification or unit, the assessor and the period, and the percentage you will sample. 10 to 20% is usual for routine sampling.
Sample and give a verdict: Open a plan, add observations or off-the-job entries to the sample and mark each one agree, disagree or refer back.
Raise and close actions: A disagree or refer becomes a finding with an action plan and a due date. Close it with a note once it is resolved.
Standardise: Record each standardisation meeting with attendees, decisions and actions, so every assessor is marking to the same standard.
notes: The EQA visit pack: Downloads a ZIP of the last 12 months: plans, verdicts, findings, meetings and coverage, ready for the external quality assurer.
Coverage: The coverage tab shows which units and assessors have been sampled, so gaps in the plan are easy to see.

helps.title: A sampling plan
helps.what: One IQA sampling plan: the assessor decisions you have picked to check, your verdict on each, and any actions raised from them.
steps: Pick what to sample: Add the assessor's assessment decisions, observations or verified off-the-job entries from the lists below, one at a time or a handful at random. Each one counts toward the plan's percentage.

Give a verdict: Mark each sample agree, disagree or returned, and add a short rationale. On a decision, agree confirms it for the learner and returned sends it back. On a keyboard, focus a sample and press 1 to 4.
Returned work: Disagree or returned opens an action for the assessor and tells them, with a link to the learner. They close it once they have looked again.
Raise a finding: For anything wider than one decision, raise a finding with the details filled in, so it gets an action plan, an owner and a due date.
Close the loop: Close findings on the IQA dashboard once they are resolved. The plan is done when the target is met and every action is closed.
notes: View evidence: Opens the file the assessor or apprentice attached, so you check the same evidence the decision was based on. For a decision it opens the learner's Assess section.
Never your own work: You cannot sample or give a verdict on a decision you made yourself.
New assessors: A plan for an assessor in their first six months is set to 100%.

helps.title: A learner’s evidence pack
helps.what: Everything the funding rules need on file for this apprentice, plus your college’s own requirements, checked live against the record.
steps: Work down the orange: Each item says what is needed, which paragraph of the rules asks for it, and its status.
File or fix: Tap File to add the document and who signed it, Edit details for the ULN, NI number and dates, or open reviews and hours where those items live.
Download for an audit: Download the pack gives an A4 PDF with every item, document, version and signature, ready to hand over.
Record breaks and changes: A break in learning, a new employer, withdrawal or completion goes in the programme history, with the last day of evidenced learning.
notes: New versions, never overwrites: Filing again keeps the old document and marks it replaced. Every file keeps a fingerprint showing it has not been altered.

helps.title: Delivering a lesson
helps.what: The presenter view for the class: one activity at a time in big type, with a countdown for each that moves on by itself when it reaches zero.
steps: Start: Press Play (or the space bar). The ring counts down the activity; the bar at the top shows the whole session.
Move through it: Next and Prev (or the arrow keys) change activity. Tap a segment of the bar to jump straight to it.
Take the register: Register in the top bar opens the class register with the cohort and date filled in.
notes: Keys: Space play or pause, arrows move, R resets the timer, F full screen, Esc goes back to the plan.

helps.title: A lesson plan
helps.what: One lesson from start to finish: what learners will be able to do, the timed session, your briefing, how you will check learning, and the criteria it covers.
steps: Check it: Read the objectives and the session timings. Tap Rewrite on any section to have it redrafted, then keep or discard the suggestion.
Get ready: Build the slides, download a PDF copy, and schedule it for a cohort, date and room.
Teach it: Deliver opens the presenter view. Register takes attendance for the cohort in two taps.
Close it off: Mark it ready before the class and delivered after it. The button at the top always shows the next step; Duplicate and Delete are under More.
notes: Rewrites: A rewrite is drafted by AI from the plan and the regulations it cites. Nothing changes until you accept it.

helps.title: Slides for a lesson
helps.what: A slide deck built from the lesson plan, ready to present here or download as PowerPoint.
steps: Build it: Build the deck and choose how many slides, the tone and the depth. Photos are added after the text.
Check and edit it: Tap a slide to open it. Change the heading and notes in place, open the full editor for the rest, or ask for that one slide to be redone with a note.
Present it: Present opens full screen. Arrow keys or a swipe move between slides. Press N for your notes, the next slide and a clock. Press T to start an activity timer.
Take it with you: Download PowerPoint gives you a file with your speaker notes in it.
notes: How it is made: Slide text and photos are drafted by AI from the lesson plan and the regulation extracts linked to it. Regulation slides paraphrase their source and name it. Check every slide before you teach from it.

helps.title: Marking
helps.what: Written answers on your quizzes. Each one is pre-scored against your mark scheme; you read it, change the score if you disagree, and sign it off. Nothing counts until you do.
steps: Quizzes you set: Every attempt on a quiz you created lands here, whichever cohort the learner is in. "Needs a human mark" shows only the ones with written answers still to sign off; "Everything" shows auto-marked ones too. The switch at the top (Mine, My cohorts, Whole college) narrows it to those learners.
Start at the top: The attempt that has waited longest comes first. Over a week is orange.
Open and mark: Tap Mark to read each answer with its suggested score. Change any score, add feedback, and approve.
Approve several at once: Tick attempts whose suggested scores you accept and press Approve. Every answer on them is signed off at that score.
Use the keyboard: On a computer: j and k move, Enter opens, Shift+A approves, x ticks, Esc clears.
Suggested marks use AI: An AI model reads each written answer against your mark scheme and suggests a score with its reasons. It is a suggestion: you change it or approve it.
notes: Still to score: Answers not pre-scored yet. Suggest marks runs the AI scoring for every one; you still sign each off.

helps.title: The Ofsted lens
helps.what: A live read of your evidence against the evaluation areas Ofsted now inspects further education and skills providers on. It shows where your records are strong and where an inspector would find gaps. It does not predict a grade.
steps: Start with the red and orange areas: Each area shows how ready your evidence is. Open the rows inside it to go straight to the records behind the figure.
Close the gaps: Known gaps are things the app does not track yet. Keep that evidence somewhere you can show an inspector, or log an action in the improvement plan.
Download it for the nominee: Download PDF gives a snapshot for your nominee or senior leaders before a visit.
notes: How Ofsted grades now: Each area is graded on five points: exceptional, strong standard, expected standard, needs attention, urgent improvement. Safeguarding is met or not met. There is no overall effectiveness grade from November 2025.

Whole provider and provision type: Safeguarding, inclusion, leadership and governance, and contribution to meeting skills needs are judged for the college as a whole. Curriculum, teaching and training, achievement, and participation and development are judged for each type of provision, such as apprenticeships.

helps.title: Quality thresholds
helps.what: The numbers the hub uses to judge: when attendance is low, how much IQA should sample, how far back inspection signals look, and how an EPA readiness score becomes a verdict.
steps: Change a number: Each field says what it drives and its default. Nothing changes until you save.
Save: Saved for the whole college. Every screen in the hub picks it up within a second.
Start again: Reset to defaults puts every field back to the standard values; save to keep them.
notes: EPA bands: A readiness score from 0 to 100 falls into one band. Bands should run end to end with no gaps, from 0 up to 100.

Risk flags: At the bottom: the signs that add to a learner's risk score, and the score for medium, high and critical. They have their own Save and are used from the next nightly check, or straight away with Recheck risk now.

helps.title: Hours to verify
helps.what: Off-the-job hours your apprentices have logged and sent to you. Verified hours count on their record and in the funding evidence; returned ones go back to the learner with your note.
steps: Start at the top: The oldest entry comes first. Anything over a week is orange: unverified hours start to cost the learner.
Read and decide: Open an entry to see what they did, their photos and a suggested check. Verify it, or Return it with a note saying what to add.
Clear several at once: Tick the entries you are happy with and Verify them together, or Return them all with one shared note.
Use the keyboard: On a computer: j and k move, Enter opens, Shift+V verifies, r returns, x ticks, Esc clears.
notes: Mine, My cohorts or Whole college: The switch in the bar at the top sets this for the whole College Hub. Mine is the apprentices assigned to you, My cohorts is everyone in the cohorts you teach. With nobody of yours, you see everyone.
The suggested check: It reads the entry and says whether it looks complete. It never verifies anything for you.

helps.title: A college policy
helps.what: One policy: what it says, who owns it, when it is next reviewed, and which staff have read and signed the current version.
steps: Edit the draft: Tap Edit to change the wording. The preview shows how staff will see it. Editing a live policy turns it back into a draft; the live version stays in the history untouched.
Publish a version: Publishing freezes this wording as a new version and asks every member of staff to acknowledge it again.
Chase signatures: The sign-off log shows who has acknowledged the current version and who has not.
notes: Archiving: An archived policy stays in the version history but nobody is asked to sign it. You can restore it at any time.

helps.title: Quality improvement plan
helps.what: Every action the college has agreed to improve quality, from the self-assessment, inspections and IQA. Each has an area, a priority, a target date and a state.
steps: Add an action: Say what will change and why, pick the area it improves, set a priority and a target date.
Move it on: Tap Move on as work progresses: planned, in progress, completed. Completed is the end. Tap Blocked when something outside your control is stopping it, and Move on when it is unblocked.
Watch the overdue count: Anything past its target date and not completed shows in orange. That is what an inspector will ask about.
notes: Areas: Areas follow Ofsted’s renewed framework from November 2025: safeguarding, inclusion, leadership and governance, contribution to meeting skills needs, curriculum, teaching and training, achievement, and participation and development. Use “Across areas” for an action that touches several.

helps.title: Reports
helps.what: Every export a funding auditor, awarding body, inspector or head of department might ask for: ready-made PDFs, and spreadsheets you can open in Excel.
steps: Pick a report: Ready-made PDFs download straight away. The spreadsheets are grouped by what they are for: funding and audit, progress and achievement, and curriculum.
Narrow it down: Choose a cohort, a date range or a qualification where the report allows it, then tap Run report.
Check, then download: The figures and chart summarise exactly the rows you will download. The first 25 rows show below so you can check before you send it.
notes: Opening in Excel: Downloads include a marker so Excel shows pound signs and accented names correctly.
Other exports: Each quiz also has its own export on the Quizzes page.

helps.title: Self-assessment report
helps.what: A first draft of your annual self-assessment, written from what the college already records: attendance, achievement, end-point assessment, IQA and staff. You read and challenge it, send it for review, and an admin or head of department approves it.
steps: Generate the draft: Mate reads your live records and writes a summary, strengths, areas for improvement and a section for each Ofsted evaluation area, with a self-assessed grade and its evidence.

Read and challenge it: Open each section and check every figure against the evidence. The draft itself is not edited here: if something is wrong, correct the record it came from and regenerate the draft.
Send for review, then approve: Only an admin or head of department can approve. An approved draft is locked; if things change, start a new draft and the approved one stays in the history.
Look back at older drafts: Every draft stays under All drafts. Tap one to read it; older drafts open read-only.
Turn weaknesses into actions: Every area for improvement should become an action in the quality improvement plan, with an owner and a date.
notes: The new Ofsted framework: Ofsted now inspects further education and skills on evaluation areas, not the old five judgements: safeguarding, inclusion, leadership and governance, contribution to meeting skills needs, and for each type of provision, curriculum, teaching and training, achievement, and participation and development. Safeguarding is met or not met; the rest use five grades from exceptional to urgent improvement. There is no overall grade. Drafts made before October 2026 keep their old headings and show where each now sits.

helps.title: A quiz
helps.what: How the group did on one quiz: who has done it, the average and pass rate, which questions and criteria tripped them up, and every attempt.
steps: Publish it: A draft is hidden from learners. Publish it when it is ready; every learner it is for gets a notification that opens the quiz. Unpublish to take it back.
Set it again: Send a fresh copy with the same questions to a cohort with a new due date, for a retake or next year's group. Earlier attempts stay here.
Find the weak spots: Criteria and questions are ranked by how many got them right. Tap a weak criterion to send a follow-up quiz on it.
Mark and review: Tap an attempt to see every answer. Written answers get a suggested mark for you to confirm or change. When every written answer is signed off, the learner gets their final result.
Another tutor's quiz: You can see any quiz set at your college. Only the tutor who set it, or a college admin, publishes or marks it.

helps.title: Quizzes and assessments
helps.what: Every quiz, assessment and mock exam you have set, with how many learners have done it, the average score and the pass rate.
steps: Set one: New quiz drafts the questions from BS 7671 and the qualification criteria for a cohort or one learner. Check them, then publish.
Check the written answers: Written answers get a suggested mark. Open the marking queue to confirm or change each one.
Chase and review: Overdue shows homework past its due date. Open a quiz to see each learner's attempt and the hardest questions.
notes: Export: Export CSV downloads the list as it is filtered, for a quality review or a team meeting.

helps.title: Your day
helps.what: What today holds for you: your classes, everything waiting on you from the inbox, learners the risk check has flagged, and what is coming up this week.
steps: Check your classes: Today’s classes, yours first. Tap one to open the lesson and take the register.
Clear what needs you: Hours to verify, evidence to assess, replies, IQA and reviews, oldest first. The button says what to do and opens the exact item.
Look after flagged learners: Register, add a note or look at their evidence without leaving the page.
notes: Mine, My cohorts or Whole college: The switch at the top picks whose work you see, for the whole College Hub. Pick Whole college to cover for a colleague.
Same list as the inbox: Needs you is the college inbox, so its count matches the bell and the inbox page.

helps.title: Your inbox
helps.what: Everything at your college that needs a tutor, in one list: hours, app learning, evidence, comments, messages, IQA, progress reviews, check-ins and marking. Each one opens exactly where it is done, and leaves the inbox when it is.
steps: Start at the top: Anything that has waited too long comes first, marked orange. A learner’s hours and evidence start to cost them after a week.
Open and act: The button says what to do: Verify, Assess, Reply, Book. It takes you straight to that item, not just the learner.
Narrow it down: Pick a kind on the left, a cohort or how long it has waited, or search for a learner. The switch at the top picks Mine, My cohorts or Whole college for the whole College Hub.

Do several at once: Tick rows to verify hours or mark them seen together. On a desktop: j and k move, Enter or v opens, Shift+V verifies hours, r replies, x ticks. On a phone, swipe right for the button’s action and left to mark seen.
notes: The same list everywhere: The home page’s Needs you and the bell read this list, so the counts always match.

helps.title: Courses from your firm
helps.what: Study Centre courses your firm has asked you to do, with the date they need them by.
steps: Start the course: Tap Start course. It opens in the Study Centre, where you work through it at your own pace.
Pass the final paper: Each course ends with a final mock paper. Tap Take the final paper when you are ready. Passing it is what marks the course done.
Your firm sees it: They're told straight away, and if you have an Elec-ID it's added there as a Study Centre course. Nothing to send.
notes: Is it the qualification?: No. A Study Centre course is learning (CPD). It does not replace a certificate from an awarding body, such as the City & Guilds 2382.

helps.title: Right to work
helps.what: Every firm must check that the people who work for it are allowed to work in the UK. This page sends your details to the office so they can do the check.
steps: Get a share code: If you have an eVisa or settled status, get a share code on gov.uk ("Prove your right to work to an employer"). It starts with W.
Or photograph your documents: A British or Irish passport, or the documents the office asks for. They still need to see the originals with you.
Send it: The office checks it and records the check. Only the owner and admins can see what you send.

helps.title: Your timesheets
helps.what: Your hours for each day, sent to the office to approve. Approved hours are what you are paid for.
steps: Clock in when you start: Pick the job and tap Clock in. If location is on, the office sees where you clocked in.
Clock out when you finish: Check your break minutes and tap Clock out. The day goes to the office to approve.
Missed a day?: Use Add a past day. If the office sends a day back, fix it and send it again.

helps.title: Everyone on the board
helps.what: Every learner on the leaderboard, with their XP today, this week, this month, this year and all time side by side.
steps: Pick a period, then what to rank by: Period sets the window: today, this week, this month, this year or all time. Rank by sets the order: XP (the same ranks as the leaderboard), days studied in that period, or current streak. On a computer you can also tap any column heading.
Find someone: Search by name, or tap “Find me” to jump to your own row.

Read the figures: Days is how many days someone studied in the period you picked (on Today, it shows this week). Periods run on UK time: weeks start Monday, months on the 1st. Awards only count towards all time.

helps.title: Leaderboard and XP
helps.what: Everyone’s XP for the month, the week or all time. Monthly competitions are decided on the month board: XP earned from the 1st to the last day of the month, UK time.
steps: Earn XP: Mock exams, quizzes, course sections, flashcards and more. Every rule is listed under “How XP is earned”.
Check your place: Your card shows your XP this period, your rank and how far you are behind the next person.
See every point: “Your XP” lists every award and what earned it, including the ones that didn’t count and why.
notes: Fair play: XP is worked out by the server, not your phone. Each quiz, paper and section earns once per day, and there is a cap of … XP a day. Repeats and double taps earn nothing.
Ties: Two people on the same XP are ranked by who got there first.
Not on the board?: You need a name on your profile and your leaderboard setting switched on. Staff and test accounts are never ranked.

helps.title: Mock exams
helps.what: Every practice paper built into your courses, in one place, timed and marked against the real pass mark.
steps: Pick a paper: Filter by track or search by course, qualification number or topic. Each sitting draws a fresh set of questions from the course bank, so you can sit the same paper again and get a different set.
See how you did: Every sitting is saved to your history: your score against the pass mark, the topics that cost you marks, and the questions you got wrong.
Revise what you got wrong: Wrong answers go on your revision pile and come back until you get them right. A weak spots mock builds a paper from the topics you find hardest.

helps.title: Mock exam history
helps.what: Everything you’ve sat, on any device: mock exams, topic tests and AM2 practice. How each paper is going, your strongest and weakest topics, and what to do next.
steps: What you’ve done: Every sitting, how many passed and your study rhythm over the last 12 weeks.
Where you are: The paper you’re working on, with a pass forecast from your last three sittings, then a verdict for every paper.
How to get better: Your weakest topics across everything you’ve sat. Study opens the lesson; Practise drills those questions.
Open any sitting: Attempts lists every sitting. Recent mocks show each question you got wrong; older ones show how you did by topic.

helps.title: Your course
helps.what: Every module of your Study Centre course: how much you’ve studied and how your mock questions on its topics have gone.
steps: See the whole course: Each module shows the sections you’ve finished and your mock accuracy on its topics.
Find the weak modules: Orange means under 60% right. Open a module to see which topics are dragging it down.
Close the gaps: Continue the module, practise its weakest topic, or ask Dave to explain it.

helps.title: The Study Centre
helps.what: Courses, mock exams and revision in one place. The top of the page tells you how you are doing and what to do next; everything you do here counts towards your streak and level.
steps: Check your figures: Your streak, your mock average against the pass mark, and how many questions are due to revise.
Do the next thing: “What to do next” is ranked for you: unfinished sections, weak topics and anything due.
Work on your weak spots: “How to get better” shows your weakest topics from your mocks, with a lesson to study and questions to practise for each.
Revise what you got wrong: Every question you get wrong in a mock comes back after a day, three days and a week. Get it right each time and it’s learned.
notes: Streaks and freezes: Any study on a day (UK time) keeps your streak. Every 7 days in a row earns a streak freeze (you can hold 2); miss a day and one is used automatically so the streak carries on.
What the colours mean: Green is a pass or a strong topic. Orange is below the pass mark or a topic to work on.
